cases.name: 92 & 94 Round Hill Road (golf greens/tees)
cases.applicant: Michael Lehrer (owner, 92 Round Hill Road) and Round Hill Land Corp (owner, 94 Round Hill Road); attorney Jerry Tortorella of Hocherman Tortorella & Wexler; engineer Tim Allen of Go Associates

trajectory.status: public hearing continued / adjourned to first meeting in September
public hearing continued / adjourned to October 27

timeline.status: public hearing continued / adjourned to first meeting in September
timeline.summary: This continued hearing addressed after-the-fact legalization of golf improvements (one remaining green, sand traps, four tees, and paths) partly within a wetland and its buffer, some built without permits. The applicant argued the use is a customary residential accessory use, that setbacks for pools/tennis courts do not apply, that tees T2-T4 are just movable turf with no disturbance, and that there has been no incident in 26 years. Neighbor Barry Edelman (88 Round Hill Road) and his attorney strongly opposed on safety grounds (errant balls toward a glass-walled house, grandchildren, the road) and urged setbacks, DEC review, a net, and reorienting/relocating the green. The board reached consensus to keep the 1999-approved T1 and T2 but eliminate the later-added T3 and T4, require a detailed landscape/mitigation plan (screening trees plus possibly a golf net), seek a building-inspector zoning determination, and direct the applicant to file with the DEC. The green will stay in its current location (moving it would require ~100 cubic yards of fill and wetland disturbance).

timeline.status: public hearing continued / adjourned to October 27
timeline.summary: Reopened/re-noticed hearing on site plan, wetlands and tree-removal permits to renovate and consolidate private golf greens and tees. The applicant eliminated two new tees, added a buffer/screening plan (12 trees, 54 shrubs, 100 ground covers) and a DEC validation block, and offered a golf pro to argue the short-hole shots pose little risk given 25+ years without incident. Neighbors and their counsel pressed safety concerns about golf balls crossing property lines and asked for netting, a fence, deflector walls and a building-inspector use/setback determination. Because of the short board no vote could be taken; the board discussed deflector screens near the tee boxes as mitigation and adjourned to October 27, leaving the hearing open.

At the very start of the meeting the Chair confirmed no one was present for 92 & 94 Round Hill Road and announced the public hearing had been moved off the agenda for the night, to be covered on another date. No substantive discussion occurred. The item was carried to a future meeting.

The applicant's principal could not attend, so the board reopened and then adjourned the hearing to the second January meeting (Jan 26, 2026) at counsel's request. Counsel noted revised plans that removed the lower 'T' structure entirely, and a neighbor's attorney (George Ellison, for Barry Edelman at 88 Round Hill Road) offered constructive administrative comments: correcting drawing revision dates, papering the T removal in a whereas clause, adding an as-built and an anti-expansion (null-and-void) condition, and exploring whether netting should also run across the top of T2. The board was amenable and set the continued date.

cases.name: 7 Hollow Ridge Road
cases.address: 7 Hollow Ridge Road (Wood Hollow Estates, ~2.5 acre lot)
cases.applicant: Represented by Ralph Alpinsetti; owner/builder John Nickett

timeline.summary: A vacant lot from a 1999-2000 subdivision, no wetlands, with public sewer and well water, proposed for a ~7,500-8,000 sq ft house comparable to neighbors. Discussion focused on extensive cut/fill, whether retaining walls could reduce cutting, tree-removal mitigation via landscaping, a rock outcrop that may allow steeper cuts, and building-height rules (average-grade vs lowest-grade measurement) affecting a desired walkout basement. The builder cited prior successful projects on Terrace Circle. The board directed responses to staff memos, a staff meeting, and scheduling a public hearing.

Continuation of a public hearing for a single-family house with a proposed pool, patio, driveway and stormwater mitigation. The applicant reported reducing disturbance from ~71,700 to ~62,000 sq ft, adding a rear retaining wall, and cutting tree removals from 134 to 99. Most of the session walked through the town engineer's (John Kellard's) memo, which the applicant had not yet seen: grading of a rear knoll, up-to-10-foot driveway cuts and rock, sediment/erosion control (a temporary sediment trap instead of just silt fence), and trench drains on the 14% driveway. Board decided the applicant should take the memo home, revise the plans, and return for a final resolution; the hearing was adjourned but left open.

Resumed public hearing on a site plan with significant grading and drainage. The applicant's team recounted a productive Zoom meeting with town engineer John Kellard resolving erosion-control, sediment-basin sequencing, trench-drain sump structure and driveway water-bar issues, and proposed removing a rear retaining wall and consolidating drainage to the front. Roughly 22 trees may be removed pending final cut/fill analysis near drip lines. A neighbor concern was addressed via a resolution condition for 20 new Green Giant arborvitae screening. The Chair declined to approve because the revised plans were not yet formalized and the tree impacts undefined, sending the applicant back to perfect the drawings with the engineer before returning.

Continuation of a public hearing on a residential site plan. An enhanced landscaping plan (21 green giant arborvitae in the rear versus the 20 requested) was submitted, and the engineer's memos and comments were resolved. Tree removal to be shown at drip lines increased from 99 to 131 trees, and the site must be stabilized before framing; a well permit was obtained from the Health Department. Board members had no further questions, so the Chair closed the public hearing and adopted the site plan resolution.

cases.name: 250 East Middle Patent Road
cases.applicant: Neil & Vanessa Lucy (owners); attorney Michael Sirignano; landscape architect Jerry Barrett; Nicholas Sarai / Hudson Engineering

timeline.summary: A returning application (last seen ~5 years ago under prior owners) for a pool. The applicant presented a new sketch pushing the pool back 16 feet and dropping it about 4 feet so it sits in the side yard on the 75-foot setback line rather than the front yard, eliminating the zoning variance while still requiring scenic-road-overlay and wetland-buffer (150-foot buffer, 25% slopes) attention. The board strongly favored the revised concept, noting it ties the patio to the pool and screens better. They directed the team to formalize the plans with a landscape plan and wetland mitigation plan and return.

Following a recent site walk, Michael Cerniano presented Jerry Barrett's revised plan, which pulls the structure 16 feet further from the road and roughly 18 feet lower in elevation so it is essentially not visible; it is also no longer in the front yard. The board viewed this favorably and discussed the wetland permit trigger (within 150 feet of a wetland) and a steep-slope question, with the engineer clarifying the 25% slope rule. The board voted to refer the applicant to the Conservation Board, after which a public hearing and draft resolution would follow. A public hearing is anticipated in September.

Site plan to install a swimming pool along East Middle Patent Road, a designated scenic road. After board feedback at a site walk, the applicant moved the pool back 16 feet and four feet lower in elevation to avoid a variance, keeping the pool just outside the 75-foot front-yard setback (edge of water ~79 feet). Board members agreed the topography and landscaping would screen the pool from the scenic road, praised the collaborative redesign, closed the hearing, and approved the site plan.

cases.name: 154 Lafayette Avenue parking discussion
cases.applicant: Applicant with representative 'Mark' (contractor business with truck fleet)

timeline.summary: Extended discussion of a site plan for a truck-based business needing outdoor truck storage (19 truck spots) plus employee/office parking. The police department objected to newly created front spaces that would require vehicles to back out into the Lafayette Avenue right-of-way, unlike existing grandfathered conditions elsewhere. The board explored alternatives with staff: parallel parking in front, moving the retaining wall, angled parking, and stacking trucks so drivers park in the truck space. Member Steve Sorrell argued the low-intensity, once-a-day traffic and good sight distance weigh against the safety concern, while the engineer noted the offset between pavement and property line makes parallel parking impractical. No decision; the applicant was asked to produce a revised parallel-parking plan and a narrative to bring back to the police, and to relocate the ADA spaces nearer the accessible ramp.

Discussion of establishing an office, merging lots and moving a lot line to park US-mail delivery trucks. The core debate was parking configuration: the applicant preferred perpendicular street parking (yielding ~17 spaces) so drivers arriving 3-5 a.m. could park and grab trucks without a 'demolition derby,' but the police recommended against it and town code prohibits it (neighbors' perpendicular parking was grandfathered via ZBA variances/town-board licenses). The applicant, who felt singled out, ultimately deferred to the board. Larry and new member Tom favored respecting the police and using the presented six parallel spaces; Steve and Christopher saw merit in perpendicular. The board directed the applicant to move the current parallel-parking plan forward and scheduled it for a public hearing rather than sending him to the ZBA.

Change of use of a legal non-conforming home to office use, with a related lot-line/subdivision consolidating three parcels (removing one dwelling, moving a property line). The recurring sticking point had been parking, especially six parallel spaces at the street plus 16 truck-storage spaces in back. Board confirmed no exterior changes (so no ARB needed) and worked through whether ZBA relief was required, concluding the non-conformity isn't being increased (a building-inspector determination). The condition to show nine required off-street office spaces (kept truck-free) was refined, an ARB condition struck, and the board adopted the negative declaration plus site plan and preliminary/final subdivision resolutions.

cases.name: 76 Virginia Road (rock-cut / retaining-wall development)
cases.applicant: Tony Vinesiano (owner/attorney) with engineer Jose Rodriguez, Sessie Consulting Engineers

trajectory.status: public hearing continued (kept open/adjourned); Negative Declaration adopted as amended

timeline.summary: Discussion of a major rock-excavation project after the town's peer-review geotechnical engineer (Carlin Simpson) reported ~99% of requested data now provided. The engineer detailed 21 test pits, 8 borings, geophysical scanning of fractures, line-drilling and rock-splitting (no blasting) in controlled 10-foot lifts, and a ring-net/rock-bolt drapery system with pins 15-25 ft deep over a 3-4 month duration. Members probed safety and what happens if something is missed, oversight during construction, and monitoring (vibration sensors, existing-condition surveys). Counsel raised the need for a proper SEQR review (unlisted action - a full EAF was agreed) and a possible ZBA revisit because the variance predated SEQR. The board agreed to schedule a public hearing (targeting Dec 8) with the geotechnical engineer present.

timeline.status: public hearing continued (kept open/adjourned); Negative Declaration adopted as amended
timeline.summary: The applicant returned on the proposal to cut into a rock hillside behind an office building, submitting a Phase 1A archaeological report (no/low sensitivity, accepted by SHPO) to resolve the historic-value question. Extensive deliberation covered a required seismic/vibration monitoring plan, perpetual maintenance via a deed restriction and bond, and staging of an estimated 20 trucks/day for months on Virginia Road. Two residents spoke critically: the North Castle Historical Society flagged an inaccurate letter reference in the Negative Declaration (removed by amendment), and Vincent Giordano challenged anchor lengths, ice/safety, and whether the project is really a rock quarry. The board adopted the amended Negative Declaration but kept the public hearing open, directing the applicant to bring back a written monitoring plan for the town engineer's review, a truck-staging plan, and bonding/insurance details for repair/repinning.

Resumed public hearing on a 0.94-acre, ~15,700 sf building for a landscaping business (indoor truck/equipment parking plus office), requiring a large rock cut with 70-foot cuts, a stabilized rock wall (chipping, not blasting; not crushing on site) and a truck-routing plan queuing trucks off-site. The board dwelled at length on insurance/liability for potential future wall or slope failure, concluding contractor, engineer and owner policies apply and that the residual risk is covered via the operating agreement/maintenance manual traveling with the deed, with a 'reasonable' insurance requirement to be baked into the building department's operating permit. It reviewed the upgraded seismic/vibration/air/noise monitoring plan (stop-work exceedance alerts emailed to the town's building and engineering departments and Carlin Simpson) and a Phase 1B archaeology report finding no sensitivity on-site (with notable Battle of White Plains findings on the adjacent Miller Hill Park). The board closed the hearing and adopted the draft resolution as amended, referencing the new Phase 1B document.

cases.name: 1613 Old Orchard Street
cases.applicant: Attorney Wolfson (Hopperman Tortarella & Wexler) for owners Marlene Duran & Diane Rosenberg; engineer Ralph

timeline.summary: This long-running application (before the board since January 2023) seeks site plan approval and a wetland permit for a single-family home on a vacant lot largely within the regulated wetland buffer. The applicant recounted the procedural history: Conservation Board approval with conditions (reduce footprint, obtain DEC approval), a ~500 sq ft footprint reduction, ARB design approval, and a June ZBA site-distance variance for the driveway. Building and impervious coverage were shown to fall within the range of surrounding lots. Members found the design (a center-hall colonial with front-facing garage) in keeping with the area, while the town engineer raised remaining comments on basement elevation/drainage and clarity of tree removal. The next step is scheduling the public hearing with neighbor notification.

Site plan, tree removal, and wetlands permit for a new two-story four-bedroom colonial (~3,000 sq ft living area, ~4,000 sq ft gross) with a two-car garage on a vacant lot; nearly all disturbance is in the wetland buffer, none in the wetland itself. A neighbor's engineer raised three concerns: whether stormwater design accounted for climate change per the 2024 DEC manual, that the building coverage remained among the largest in the neighborhood despite a 512 sq ft reduction, and driveway sight-line/blind-hill safety. The board treated the driveway as conforming (200-foot sight line plus a ZBA variance), found the footprint reasonable for new construction and consistent on impervious coverage, and, noting the home's 10 Cultec infiltrators exceed neighbors' stormwater controls, closed the hearing and approved a slightly amended resolution conditioned on the DEC wetland permit.

cases.name: 18 Long Pond Road (pool/spa in wetland buffer)
cases.applicant: Dean Poishler, landscape architect, for owners Daniel and Joanna

trajectory.status: referred back / discussion; public hearing to be scheduled (November)

timeline.status: referred back / discussion; public hearing to be scheduled (November)
timeline.summary: Referred back to the Planning Board after a split Conservation Board vote (4 of 7 members present). The applicant substantially scaled down the plan in response to conservation comments: pool reduced to 17x37 (~25%), patio cut close to 50%, wetland setback increased from ~12 to ~19 feet, and mitigation plantings raised from two-to-one to three-to-one to enhance a low-functioning wetland. Conservation liaison Jane Black explained two members favored the enhanced mitigation while two objected (one over a culvert/former stream bed under the pool, one over the small yard). Engineer John Kellard and the board viewed it as a net positive for the wetland buffer. The board signaled support, treating optional amenities in a wetland buffer as acceptable where there is a net benefit, and directed the applicant to schedule a public hearing (likely November).

The board opened a public hearing on a site plan, tree removal permit and wetlands permit for a swimming pool, patio and amenities within a regulated wetland buffer. Landscape architect Dean Pushlar described extensive wetland pockets connected by an old 24-inch pipe, no direct wetland disturbance (work is in existing lawn), removal of diseased beech trees, a stormwater detention/slow-release design, and 3-to-1 mitigation planting to convert a low-functioning wetland into a higher-functioning one. A conservation board member ('John') explained the board's 2-2 split: all agreed the mitigation and planting were positive, but some members did not want to reward additional work on land that historically held a watercourse before a pipe was installed decades ago, while others saw it as a net ecological improvement. Board members probed the pipe's condition (scoped and functioning), water flow/topography, and the drawdown practice. The board closed the hearing and approved the site plan, wetland and tree removal permits.

cases.name: 100 Buck Out Road (new dwelling)

timeline.summary: Discussion of a new ~3,700 sq ft house on an existing lot (replacing the existing dwelling, keeping a cottage), referred to the planning and conservation boards by the RPRC due to steep-slope, wetland-buffer and grading impacts. The engineer corrected the tree count (two removals, not seven, mostly dead) and explained ~10,830 sq ft of steep-slope disturbance is largely bare rock outcropping, with the septic location constrained by wetland buffers on both sides. The applicant offered to reduce rock removal from ~12 ft to 4-5 ft by eliminating a walkout door to lessen disturbance near the wetlands, which the board welcomed. The board scheduled a combined site walk for Nov 19 at 8:30 a.m. and referred the application to the conservation board.

This was a continuation of a public hearing on a wetlands permit that the board had previously been reluctant to approve as a minor wetlands permit, so the applicant had been directed to the Conservation Board. The Conservation Board (represented by liaison Jane/Vincent) reviewed the home mitigation plan, found the structure could not be moved out of the buffer, and approved a mitigation plan providing slightly more than two-to-one. The applicant also reached out to SHIPO regarding the nearby African American historic cemetery and received a response of no impact. A previously missing page of engineering conditions was now reflected in the draft resolution, and the board closed the hearing and approved the resolution.

cases.applicant: Our Monk LLC; Andrew Vekarello (representative), owner present (introduced himself), from 32 Orchard Drive

timeline.summary: Public hearing opened for a new four-bedroom single-family dwelling with three-car garage on Lot 1 of the previously approved 32 Orchard Drive subdivision, replacing an existing tennis court and including septic, well, driveway, and stormwater (shared BMP plus a rain garden); 24 trees would be removed. Neighbors Darren and Susan Lampert (24 Orchard Drive), directly behind the site for 25 years, objected that removal of non-evergreen trees would expose their home to headlights and the house's height, and asked for tall evergreen screening. The applicant agreed to add staggered evergreen buffer plantings and to potentially eliminate the rear rain garden (redirecting flow to the shared BMP) to save screening trees. The board kept the public hearing open and adjourned it, asking for a revised landscape plan at the October 16th meeting.

An administrative change-of-use on the second floor with adequate existing parking. Staff (Adam Kaufman) had reviewed it and agreed the applicant did not need to formally appear. The board adopted a site-plan waiver resolution with no debate.

cases.name: 130 Old Mount Kisco Road amended final plat
cases.applicant: Corey Salomow (Zarin & Steinmetz); owner Frank Madonna / Jennifer (Keorell)

timeline.summary: A previously approved three-lot conservation subdivision needed a minor amendment: while preparing the Mylar, a 900-square-foot overlap with a neighboring property's deed was found. Rather than negotiate, the applicant shifted the line to conform to the deed, reducing the conservation area by 900 square feet while keeping Lots 1 and 2 the same size. The board found the amended final plat in substantial conformance with the preliminary plat (no hearing required) and adopted it as a de minimis change.

cases.name: 4 Vincent Lane driveway modification / site plan clean-up
cases.applicant: Tom and Sarah DeSwart (owners); Lewis Fusco, landscape architect

timeline.summary: New owners seek site-plan approval for a modified circular driveway and to memorialize prior work (a pool built under a building permit, and several sheds) that should have come to the Planning Board. The plan removes much prior turf/paved area and reduces land coverage from over 23,000 sq ft to under the approved 19,000, rewilding wetland buffers with native plantings and removing invasives; three or four sheds would be removed while two are proposed to remain. A wetland specialist flagged wetlands and the applicant is pursuing DEC jurisdiction. The board and Conservation Board liaison agreed the request is largely procedural/memorializing; the plan is to route it through the Conservation Board and continue.

cases.name: RCLA Enclave at Armonk (former MBIA campus)
cases.applicant: Kevin Moses, attorney for Toll Northeast / Toll Brothers

timeline.summary: Toll appealed an RPRC decision (prompted by ARB member Sue Geffen) that referred the applicant back to the ARB to finalize how approved color schemes would be distributed across the 125-unit site. The applicant argued the ARB's June 2024 final approval already provided for random one-third/one-third/one-third color distribution and that returning would conflict with a final approval. The board pressed on how the ARB could verify the distribution was being met. It granted the appeal with a gentleman's-agreement condition that the applicant submit a progress report (via a memo to planner Adam Kaufman) at the one-third mark rather than reappearing before the ARB.

cases.name: 12 Seymour Place East (pool, spa, cabana, carport)
cases.applicant: Lou Sousco, landscape architect, for owners Gina and Michelle
cases.lastStatus: public hearing opened / kept open; site walk scheduled

trajectory.status: public hearing opened / kept open; site walk scheduled

timeline.status: public hearing opened / kept open; site walk scheduled
timeline.summary: Public hearing on new pools, spa, patios and an oversized covered cabana/detached carport requiring a special use permit; a GLC and accessory-structure variance was already granted by the ZBA. Discussion centered almost entirely on chronic neighborhood stormwater flooding at the cul-de-sac, with Town Engineer John Kellard describing runoff originating uphill, questioning whether the existing infiltration system and diversion swale were functioning, and urging the applicant to investigate discharging the proposed runoff toward Tripling instead of Seymour Place. The applicant countered that routing to Tripling would require ~350-400 feet of trenching and removal of 50+ trees. The board directed a site walk (next Wednesday) to walk the swale and the potential Tripling route, keeping the hearing open.

cases.name: 2 Israel Townsend Hill Road (new house)
cases.address: 2 Israel Townsend Hill Road (32 Worthed Drive subdivision)
cases.applicant: Andrew Vaccarello (applicant representative)

timeline.summary: Returning after being directed to create a 'robust planting plan' to buffer the flag-lot component, the applicant presented 12 proposed trees (8 arborvitae, 4 Eastern hemlock) intermingled with existing vegetation along the concerned neighbor's property line, and removed a rain garden (saving ~8 trees) by directing drainage to a shared BMP. A confusing outdated plan link caused some frustration. Neighbor Darren Lampert argued the proposed four-foot trees were insufficient for screening/headlights. The board agreed, closed the hearing and approved the site development plan and tree-removal permit with conditions: noting the prior-night ARB approval and revising the planting schedule to 8-10 foot trees.

The applicant requested setting a public hearing and was ready to mail notices for the October 27 meeting. The board agreed to a site walk next Wednesday and to hold the hearing on the 27th.

The board approved the field change.

cases.name: 1 Israel Townsend Hill (Lot 4, 32 Orchard Drive subdivision)
cases.address: 1 Israel Townsend Hill, North Castle NY (Tax lot 108.01-6-1.4, R1A district)
cases.applicant: Andrew Vekarello for 32 Orchard Drive R-Monk LLC; owner present (ARB-approved architectural plans)

timeline.summary: The second/new house within the recently approved 32 Orchard Drive subdivision, a four-bedroom single-family dwelling on a vacant, wooded, steeply sloped lot. The applicant proposed removing eight trees, a walkout, two front retaining walls, septic and well consistent with the subdivision, and directing stormwater to the shared BMP. The home was slightly reoriented from the IPP to align with Israel Townsend Hill, which the engineer noted reduced excavation and retaining walls. Board questions covered driveway slope (~10%), perimeter foliage/screening, and line of sight of the house side from Orchard Drive. The board opened and closed the public hearing (no neighbors spoke) and adopted the resolution, handling open items administratively.

cases.name: 92 & 94 Round Hill Road (putting green and golf tees)
cases.address: 92 & 94 Round Hill Road, North Castle NY
cases.applicant: Attorney Adam Wexler with engineer Tim Allen and landscape architect Jerry Barrett, for owner Mr. Edelman; neighbor represented by attorney Judson C. of Keane & Beane PC

timeline.summary: A continued hearing on an existing private putting green and two golf tee boxes in a wetland-buffer area, focused on safety of errant golf balls reaching a neighbor's yard 16 feet from the green. The applicant proposed a localized 10-ft-wide by 6-ft-high net at the upper tee plus deflectors, and after debate agreed to also consider netting at the lower (street) tee and additional evergreen screening. The Chair raised a hypothetical concept of putting-green zoning legislation (setbacks and tee-distance limits) for the town board, which the applicant stressed does not apply to this application. Larry pressed hard that the tees should be pulled closer to the green so only chipping/pitching shots are used; the applicant argued 25 years of no incidents and topographic constraints prevent moving the upper tee. The board declined to force relocation but wanted a revised plan with netting and screening; the hearing was adjourned to November 10 for a final plan and vote.

cases.name: 12 Seymour Place East
cases.address: 12 Seymour Place East, North Castle NY
cases.applicant: Applicant with project engineer Ralph (revised drainage plan)

timeline.summary: A continued hearing over significant neighborhood drainage concerns at the end of a cul-de-sac. After engineer John Kellard and the board walked the site, the applicant presented a revised plan splitting the cultec systems so the pool/patio and the new garage each have dedicated infiltration designed to handle a 100-year storm with near-zero discharge, plus a trench drain at the driveway bottom tied into the town culvert and confirmation/replacement of an existing overflow pipe. The applicant also proposed converting ~2,000 sq ft of lawn to planted meadow and regrading/berming the rear swale toward the woodlands. The board closed the hearing and adopted the resolution as amended, relying on an existing condition that lets the town engineer police the stormwater details administratively.

cases.name: 428-436 Main Street
cases.applicant: Attorney Charles Marteban (Catania firm) for 428-436 Main Street LLC, on behalf of George Calcutini

timeline.summary: A largely procedural update to a January 2025 site plan approval. The prior approval was conditioned on providing parking for an accessory apartment; the ZBA subsequently granted a variance for 22 parking spaces, so the site plan needs to be updated to conform. The Chair asked whether the public hearing could be skipped, but it had expired and must be re-noticed. The board scheduled the public hearing and expects a resolution at the next meeting.

cases.name: 2 & 4 Massaro Court
cases.applicant: Nicholas Shari, Hudson Engineering & Consulting, for the applicants

timeline.summary: Site plan review for two proposed two-family dwellings on two lots of a recently approved three-lot subdivision. Most of the plan (driveway, utilities, stormwater) is unchanged from the approved subdivision; the buildings are new, at-grade rear terraces are being removed, and structural plans for tall retaining walls are still needed. Consultant comments require structural wall plans, protective barriers atop walls, an added parking space per unit (garage/space blocking issue), and staying under gross land coverage limits to avoid a variance. The Chair pressed strongly on the aesthetics of retaining walls up to 10-11 feet on a residential frontage, urging a tiered, more attractive design. No hearing was held; the applicant will return with revised plans, likely not the very next meeting.

cases.name: 4 Cases Court (Awesome Landscaping)
cases.applicant: John G. Scarlett Jr. (engineer) for Awesome Landscaping (office and truck/outdoor storage use)

timeline.summary: A landscaping company proposes to use an existing building for a small (~144-150 sq ft) office plus truck parking and outdoor storage in an existing lot with 51 spaces. Review comments flagged that some front parking spaces sit on town property, parking aisles are only 20 ft (not 24), and lighting and outdoor-storage layout must be addressed. The board must decide comfort with the office-to-parking relationship and the outdoor storage; a variance may ultimately be needed for aisle width. The Chair voiced support for the concept and directed the applicant to rework the lot to be as code-compliant as possible before any ZBA referral. No hearing yet.

cases.name: 22 Whippoorwill Road East (extension of time)
cases.address: 22 Whippoorwill Road East, North Castle NY
cases.applicant: Applicant/owner (not present; house nearly complete, seeking CO and property is for sale)

timeline.summary: Request for an extension of time on a site plan approval whose conditions (an easement to the town attorney's satisfaction and revised evergreen screening/landscaping along the rear property line) remain unfulfilled. A neighbor's attorney letter (for Stephen and Marian McLaughlin of 24 Whippoorwill Road East) recounted stop-work orders, a poor concrete foundation, and a pattern of disregard, urging the board to hold the applicant's feet to the fire. The board clarified the applicant cannot get a CO until the landscaping plan is submitted, approved, and installed. After debating six/four-month terms and the planting window, the board granted an extension to February 7, 2026 for the applicant to submit paperwork.

cases.name: Summit Golf Club (site plan and subdivision extensions)
cases.applicant: Summit Golf Club (Sal; water system designed by Mike Schrodtell)

timeline.summary: Status update and two extensions of time for the Summit Golf Club, which is awaiting Westchester County Health Department approval for a water system (pump station and tank) and related site elements. The engineer expects a plan to submit to the health department shortly, with everything approved at one time. The board granted an extension of time for the site plan permit and a final/eighth 90-day extension for the final subdivision plat.

cases.name: 448 Bedford Road (church nursery school)
cases.applicant: Church (additional classrooms in the nursery school)

timeline.summary: A brief, routine extension of time for a previously approved church project adding classrooms in its nursery school. The board granted the extension without discussion.

cases.name: 73 Whippoorwill Road subdivision
cases.applicant: O'Marzo Site Engineering for Wellness Estates LLC; Alex Gusky of Wellness Estates LLC present

timeline.summary: A conditions review where the board had closed the hearing but held off on approval due to numerous outstanding conditions. Working with the engineering department, the applicant reduced the preliminary plat conditions from 15 to 3 and the final subdivision conditions from 21 to 10, all of which are now items simply to be completed. The applicant agreed with the drafted October 27 resolutions. The board adopted the NEG DEC, the preliminary resolution, and the final subdivision resolution.

cases.name: 825 North Broadway (gas station renovation)
cases.address: 825 North Broadway, Armonk, NY (CB Zoning District)
cases.applicant: Owner represented by Jim Gibbons (Gibbons and Gibbons)

timeline.summary: Public hearing on renovating the interior of an existing gas station/convenience store, replacing fuel pumps and underground storage tanks, and improving circulation, stormwater, lighting and aesthetics. No public attended. Discussion focused heavily on the in-line pump layout, where a lead car fueling could block the two behind it, and whether a 'please pull forward' sign or full-service operation could ameliorate it; the applicant agreed to raise full-service with the owner. The board closed the hearing but declined to adopt the draft resolution, instead directing the applicant to address the outstanding engineering conditions (stormwater calcs, upsized pipes, ARB stone-pillar condition) and return with a far cleaner resolution before going to the building department.

cases.name: 126 Lafayette Avenue (NC Auto Repair - solar + 3-bay addition)
cases.applicant: Jamie Glover (Green Hybrid Energy Solutions) for owner Elio

timeline.summary: Site plan legitimizing the long-standing auto-repair use, adding a 48-panel/17.3kW rooftop solar array and a three-bay addition at the rear of the building, with the goal of an all-electric, net-zero facility. The panels sit only nine inches above the roofline and the adjacent Bellantoni building screens them, so no parapet wall was required. The one substantive condition was stormwater: the site currently has no runoff treatment, so the applicant agreed to a water-quality/maintenance plan (catch basins, deep-sump inlets) to the town engineer's satisfaction. Hearing was opened, closed, and the draft resolution was approved the same night.

cases.name: 258 East Middle Patent Road (Matthews accessory barn/ADU)
cases.applicant: Alan Bill (JLB Engineering) for owner Carol Matthews; architect present

timeline.summary: Discussion of establishing an accessory dwelling unit in a barn/garage building, before the board for a scenic-road location, wetland impacts and a special permit. The applicant reported the conservation board (Vincent DeAnno present) was satisfied with the wetland mitigation, having reduced buffer impacts from ~2,400 to 1,514 sq ft, with only a ~70 sq ft handicap-ramp impact plus stormwater/rain-garden work and an invasive-species removal/planting plan. Percolation testing (witnessed by the town engineer) was pending Thursday. The board called it a 'really good application,' agreed to prepare a draft resolution and schedule a public hearing (Dec 24, or Dec 8 if paperwork is ready).

The board opened and closed the public hearings for 10 and 20 Round Hill Way, which cover site plans, steep slope permits and tree removal permits (20 Round Hill Way also a special use permit) for new houses and accessory structures. These were essentially re-approvals: Adam Kaufman explained that a prior miscommunication meant the two site plans (approved earlier alongside the subdivision) never made it into the individual lot files and the resolutions had expired, so the applicant had to re-submit with minor field changes incorporated. A member asked technical questions about how Lot 5 gets access (a common driveway off Round Hill serving both lots, with an easement over the adjacent lot) and why the address faces Green Valley (E-911 routing). Both draft resolutions were adopted unanimously.

cases.name: 8 Cold Drive
cases.applicant: Corey (represented by attorney)

timeline.summary: The applicant's attorney reported that permits (clearing and grading) were pulled for a sport court, which is anticipated to be constructed in spring. The board granted an extension of time unanimously with no substantive discussion.

cases.name: Matthews Accessory Barn (258 East Middle Patten Road)
cases.applicant: Matthews (owner); Alan Piltch, engineer

timeline.summary: The board opened a public hearing on a site plan, wetland permit, scenic road and special use permit approvals for a detached accessory apartment (over 800 sq ft) in a renovated garage/barn, with a wheelchair ramp from the main house, a new septic system for the barn, a rain garden and stormwater improvements to serve an aging relative's mobility needs. Adam Kaufman confirmed the applicant had cleared the ARB, ZBA (a side-yard variance) and conservation board and addressed all planning board concerns. Much discussion focused on resolution conditions: the applicant sought (and was largely declined) to soften a 'prior to building permit' DOH/BOH condition given a dysfunctional health department, on precedent grounds; clarifying that the septic condition language ('house') applies to the barn's new system; and questioning a weekly erosion-control monitoring condition (item 10) requiring a qualified professional. The board closed the hearing and approved the site plan (Steve moved, Tom seconded, five ayes).

cases.name: 60 Cox Avenue (Breeze Mont camp)
cases.applicant: Walter (Breeze Mont summer camp)

timeline.summary: The board discussed a proposed site plan amendment to formalize on-site overflow parking (grass/lawn and side-lot spaces) for special events and staff-training days, prompted by the building department. The applicant stressed nothing changes for the regular camp season, when hundreds of attendees are still shuttled in by bus from off-site churches and temples. The board sought assurances the new spaces would not be used in-season to reduce shuttling, and asked the applicant to have its professional clearly color-code the newly added spaces versus previously approved ones on the map. The matter will proceed to a public hearing with neighbor notification.

cases.name: Orchard Subdivision (existing house access change)
cases.address: 3 (address garbled in ASR as 'Israel Council and Hill')

timeline.summary: The board reviewed a straightforward revision to the access configuration for the existing house within the Orchard five-lot subdivision (old access shown in pink, new in gray). Two of the new houses have been built; two rear lots remain to come before the board later. The change was described as very straightforward. The board agreed it still requires a public hearing with first-class-mail neighbor notification (proof of mailing, not certified) and cautioned that the notification label list may need refreshing since the moved house could pick up a different neighbor within the 250-foot radius.

cases.name: 4 Cox Court
cases.applicant: John Scarlato Jr., architect

timeline.summary: The board reviewed a revised parking plan responding to prior comments about spaces partially in the town right-of-way. The applicant will stop counting (and can remove) the encroaching spaces, restriped the existing lot with reconfigured angled/one-way aisles, and provides 41 spaces against a 30-space requirement. Adam Kaufman noted one outstanding item — a lighting plan for the previously informal lot — which the applicant has engaged someone to prepare. Board members found the design clever and workable and will bring it back for a public hearing and resolution once notice paperwork is done.

cases.name: 100 Banksville Road (sidewalk / grading)
cases.applicant: applicant with professional 'Nick' (office designer)

timeline.summary: The board discussed a sidewalk and back-grading revision from a prior site walk, where John Kellard suggested regrading approaches and a stone wall to avoid encroaching on the wetland. The applicant's professional (Nick) met with the engineer and emailed a revised plan the board had not yet seen. The board weighed whether to move to a public hearing before reviewing the new plan and getting conservation input, wary of forcing the applicant to appear at multiple hearings. Conservation chair George texted that the sidewalk work, in an already-disturbed area, is very minor and needs no conservation board review, so the board agreed to treat it as a minor wetland permit processed administratively with town engineer input, and to try to schedule the hearing.

cases.name: 76 Virginia Road (National Lawn Sprinkler / Luciano)
cases.address: 76 (74/56) Virginia Road, North White Plains; IND-A zoning district
cases.applicant: John Luciano / National Lawn Sprinkler; attorney Tony Venetano; architect Ron Horenyo; applicant engineer Jose Rodriguez; applicant geotech Carlin Simpson Associates (Bob Simpson serves as the town's retained geotech consultant)

timeline.summary: The applicant proposes a 15,000 sq ft office/warehouse building requiring a large rock and soil slope excavation (6-on-1 cuts, 25-ft rock anchors, soil nails, steel mesh netting) 12-15 ft off the property line below the Miller Hill park and battlefield. The applicant's team and the town's geotech consultant (Bob Simpson) reported the applicant met the town's review criteria and that the design is achievable, with only a minor pull-out-strength comment outstanding; the applicant agreed to a no-blasting condition (chipping only) on the site plan. Extensive public opposition and expert critique followed: residents raised fall/safety, catastrophic slope failure, aging/inadequate water and sewer, noise/dust, and the historic significance of Miller Hill, while Conservation Board member Vincent DeAnno gave a detailed technical critique (poor upper rock quality, anchors he believes are too short/undersized, corrosion-protection concerns, ice/rockfall, and long-term maintenance burden potentially falling on the town). The Open Space Committee chair (Carrie Kayza) itemized alleged misrepresentations in the applicant's environmental assessment form (SHPO/archaeology not consulted, historic and critical-environmental-area impacts unaddressed) and asked for alternatives. The board did not close the hearing; it adjourned to a future meeting to address the EAF, ongoing maintenance/deed covenants and bonding, truck logistics, and the town consultant's continuing construction-phase oversight role.

cases.name: 263 Bedford Banks Road (J. Fane equestrian property)
cases.applicant: Owner represented by attorney Jerry (J. Fane)

timeline.summary: Counsel requested a one-year extension of time on an approved equestrian estate (new residence, pool/pool house, renovated exercise barn, second stable, garage with quarters) because the volume of construction cannot be completed in the original 18-month window. The board confirmed the completion clock runs co-terminously with the building permit and granted the one-year extension. Work is reported proceeding in good faith without compliance issues.

cases.name: 4 Vincent Lane (Savage)

The Conservation Board commended the project. The board closed the public hearing but could not adopt the resolution because pre-existing sheds/barn received building permits but never got Planning Board/ARB sign-off. Sympathetic to the homeowner, the board agreed to send the applicant to the ARB and then approve at a later meeting without requiring the applicant to reappear.

cases.name: Kent Place Verizon Parking Plan expansion
cases.address: 23 Whipperwill Road East; R-3/4-acre zoning district
cases.applicant: Town of North Castle / Verizon (Kent Place parking)

timeline.summary: A re-approval: the previously approved and already-built parking project's approvals lapsed because Verizon never signed the plat map, so the board had to re-run the hearing to file with the health department. An adjacent neighbor (Suzanne) testified that Verizon fails to maintain its side of the property, left a fence down, planted no screening (the neighbor spent ~$40,000 on their own), and removed many trees without replacement, and asked for a few deciduous trees in the corner. The board explained tree replacement was not required and that the downed fence/porta-potty are building-department maintenance matters, then closed the hearing and adopted the negative declaration, site plan, and preliminary and final subdivision resolutions.

cases.name: Almonte-area residential site plan (Angela)
cases.applicant: Angela (owner); engineer absent this meeting

timeline.summary: A residential site plan revisited after prior board feedback; the applicant relocated and minimized the pool, pool house, retaining walls, and imported fill to reduce grading, and had wetlands newly flagged in the rear (coordinated between the applicant's wetlands engineer and town engineer Dave). Discussion centered on the cut/fill balance and why the house sits at elevation 473 vs a lower garage grade. The board directed the applicant to answer the planner's and town engineer's memos, meet with staff, and then schedule a public hearing. Constructive tone.

cases.name: IBM EV charger installation (corporate campus)
cases.applicant: IBM (Seth Waltzman and colleague Stephanie)

timeline.summary: IBM seeks to install EV chargers in its gated, 24/7-secured visitor lot: three Level 2 units plus one dual Level 3 (fast) charger. Town code currently limits infrastructure to Level 1/2, so the L3 needs a town-board law change (a use variance being a high bar). The board found the L3 sensible given the restricted-access, off-highway location and voted to send a memo recommending the town board amend its law to allow Level 3 charging at this site (a town-board discussion was already agendaed for that Wednesday). Conduit would run mostly above ground with minimal asphalt cutting. The board set the site-plan public hearing for its Jan 12 meeting, planning to approve both L2-only and L2+L3 scenarios.

cases.name: 12 Bedford Road
cases.applicant: Owner (the rear-access driveway project)

timeline.summary: A brief extension-of-time request on the driveway/rear-access project that is near final approval; the owner is finalizing plans and anxious to proceed. The board granted the extension.

cases.name: 4 KSL Court
cases.applicant: site engineer for the property owner (name not clearly stated)

timeline.summary: The applicant sought an amended site plan to add a landscaping-equipment/vehicle-storage tenant to an existing warehouse building that had never received formal site plan approval. Parking was reworked to eliminate off-property spaces, with dedicated spaces marked for the principal use versus the tenant, and a new lighting design was submitted to meet current code. No members of the public appeared. The board found the resolution clean and approved the amended site plan, with the lighting review satisfying condition number two.

cases.name: 62 Nethermont Avenue
cases.applicant: Rocco Delano (architect) and owners Lindsay & Dmitry; Jim New (seller/family) also spoke

timeline.summary: The applicant proposed a new ~4,865 sq ft single-family residence on an oversized R-2F lot, positioned to the south side to preserve a future subdividable lot. Neighbors, especially the Panella/Pinella family, raised concerns about rock excavation/hammering near their century-old rock-founded home, plus house size and neighborhood character; other neighbors spoke in support. The board spent most of its time debating whether to require protections beyond the town's chipping permit given the hammering would occur roughly 53-60 ft from the neighbor's foundation. After input from the applicant, an experienced contractor, and Conservation liaison Vince DeAnno, the board closed the hearing and approved the site plan with amended conditions: a seismic monitor placed on the neighbor's foundation (if they consent) and required line-drilling before chipping to reduce vibration.
The IBM EV charging station application was reached on the agenda but the applicant had removed themselves from the agenda, so no hearing or action took place.

cases.name: 100 Foxout Road
cases.applicant: Nicholas Shri, Hudson Engineering, for the applicant

timeline.summary: This R-1A application involves a site plan, wetland permit, and tree removal for a new house. Because the engineer's review memo was still far from resolved, the Chair opened and then adjourned the public hearing to let the applicant work through the memo. The applicant's engineer raised specific points on the NOI/watershed disturbance threshold, driveway drainage constrained by septic setbacks, wetland-buffer mitigation disturbance near the one-acre limit, and rock removal needed on the south side for the sunroom/walkout. The Chair advised tightening the plans and meeting with the town engineer, and noted ARB approval was still needed.

cases.name: 88 Byron Ridge Road
cases.applicant: property owner/applicant team (seeking CO); Jane (consultant) coordinated revisions

timeline.summary: This case addressed a wetland-buffer violation: additional disturbance and fill were placed during construction and a required 2022 mitigation plan had gone unimplemented for years. A previously proposed fence and 7,600 sq ft of 'no-mow' lawn were dropped, and the original mitigation plan was installed and verified by the town wetlands consultant, with boulders placed to protect the mitigation area. Conservation liaison Vince DeAnno and Lake Association president Jack expressed frustration over the delays and confusion over how the fence language reached the board's memo, but confirmed the matter was resolved with the town. The board adopted the resolution as amended, adding a clarifying 'whereas' that the fence and placed fill were removed, with five-year monitoring beginning.

cases.name: 125 Business Park Drive
cases.address: 125 Business Park Drive, Lot 5 Westchester Business Park (tax map 108.03-1-55)
cases.applicant: applicant seeking reapproval of previously approved plans

timeline.summary: The applicant sought reapproval of a previously approved (now expired) site plan for an approximately 9,390 sq ft warehouse/office commercial building with parking and loading in the PLI zoning district. The Chair read the notice, opened the public hearing, and immediately adjourned it with no substantive discussion.

cases.name: 2 & 4 Massaro Court
cases.address: Massaro Court (tax map 122.12-3-8.1 and related lots)
cases.applicant: applicant's site engineer and architect (Rick, engineer, commented)

timeline.summary: This R-2F application covers site plan and steep-slope approval for two two-family residences on adjacent Massaro Court lots. The applicant addressed prior comments by reworking the driveway retaining wall into a terraced design, adding dedicated parking so each unit has two spaces, revising side/rear grading, and clarifying footing-drain discharge. Remaining engineering memo items were deemed handleable administratively, and the town planner and engineer were comfortable. The board closed the hearings and approved the resolution for 4 Massaro Court tonight, agreeing that 2 Massaro Court (identical building) would be approved administratively at a future meeting once the applicant obtains ARB approval, with a note to watch for possible rock during the ~8 ft driveway cut.

cases.name: Virgin Mary & St. Monique Coptic Orthodox Church
cases.applicant: clergy/representatives of the Coptic Orthodox Church

timeline.summary: The church proposed a level sidewalk/walkway across its own lot to provide accessible access to the lower level of the 30-year-old church for elderly and disabled parishioners, cutting through soil behind an existing retaining wall without altering the building's exterior or the wall's appearance. The Chair asked whether an ADA ramp to the upper level was feasible; the applicants explained the upper level's many steps made that impractical, so the level walkway to the lower-level entrance is the goal. Because nothing on the building is changing, the planner concluded no ARB approval and no new variances are needed, and directed the applicant to meet with staff and schedule a public hearing.

cases.name: 850 North Broadway

meetings.meetingSummary: The board approved the June 23 minutes and then spent the bulk of the meeting on a continued public hearing for the 92 & 94 Round Hill Road golf greens/tees wetlands and site-plan application, hearing extensive neighbor testimony and directing the applicant to drop two of the four tees, submit a landscape/mitigation plan, and pursue DEC review. It briefly opened and adjourned the Mianus River Gorge hearing (applicant still needs an amended special use permit), closed and approved the U-Haul after-the-fact site plan at 1 Virginia Road with conditions, gave initial discussion and a ZBA referral to a proposed accessory barn/apartment at 58 Middle Patent Road, and approved a revised draft resolution for Four Ledgewood.

cases.name: 92 & 94 Round Hill Road (golf greens/tees)
cases.applicant: Michael Lehrer (owner, 92 Round Hill Road) and Round Hill Land Corp (owner, 94 Round Hill Road); attorney Jerry Tortorella of Hocherman Tortorella & Wexler; engineer Tim Allen of Go Associates
cases.status: public hearing continued / adjourned to first meeting in September
cases.summary: This continued hearing addressed after-the-fact legalization of golf improvements (one remaining green, sand traps, four tees, and paths) partly within a wetland and its buffer, some built without permits. The applicant argued the use is a customary residential accessory use, that setbacks for pools/tennis courts do not apply, that tees T2-T4 are just movable turf with no disturbance, and that there has been no incident in 26 years. Neighbor Barry Edelman (88 Round Hill Road) and his attorney strongly opposed on safety grounds (errant balls toward a glass-walled house, grandchildren, the road) and urged setbacks, DEC review, a net, and reorienting/relocating the green. The board reached consensus to keep the 1999-approved T1 and T2 but eliminate the later-added T3 and T4, require a detailed landscape/mitigation plan (screening trees plus possibly a golf net), seek a building-inspector zoning determination, and direct the applicant to file with the DEC. The green will stay in its current location (moving it would require ~100 cubic yards of fill and wetland disturbance).
cases.publicComment: Heavily contested. Attorney George (Keane & Beane, for Barry Edelman at 88 Round Hill Road) and Edelman himself opposed on safety, precedent, setbacks, DEC and use grounds; Antonio (100 Round Hill Road) worried about intensification/quasi-commercial use since the owner builds golf courses; a neighbor voiced seeing crowds and trucks. Heather Hart (87 Round Hill Road) spoke in support, calling the owner neighborly and saying she has never seen an errant ball in five years. George Rehmer of the Conservation Board noted four tees is more intensive than the two the CB reviewed and suggested reversing the tee/green orientation.

memberPositions.evidence: Called it 'an overreach for the planning board to start regulating this particular use in the backyard,' but pushed to eliminate T3/T4, weigh risk vs. probability, and require an enhanced landscape/net mitigation plan to abate neighbor concerns.

Questioned the green's side-yard setback (eight vs. 16 feet) and said it 'is not a wise precedent' to approve a recreational use spanning onto someone else's property, since a future owner may not own both lots.

Non-committal, wanting to explore zoning-code interpretations with counsel and the planner; argued the 'kids playing catch' analogy breaks down because of the permanence of a built installation, like a fixed pitching mound posing risk to a neighbor.

cases.name: U-Haul, 1 Virginia Road
cases.applicant: U-Haul (represented by project agent/engineer)

cases.name: Matthews accessory barn, 58 Middle Patent Road
cases.applicant: Chris Salabura and Carol Matthews (owners); engineer Allen Pilch of ALP Engineering
cases.status: discussion only / referred to ZBA (and ARB, Conservation Board)
cases.summary: The owners presented initial plans to replace a 100-plus-year-old dilapidated barn/garage with a combined garage and apartment, primarily to provide accessible space for their disabled adult son who uses a wheelchair. The Chair suggested they consider whether the existing footprint is really the best location, but accepted the owners' explanation about site constraints, easements, and neighborhood character. cases.publicComment: None; applicants noted they have already spoken with immediate neighbors who are supportive.

cases.name: Four Ledgewood
cases.summary: The board revisited a draft resolution for Four Ledgewood, a project originally approved in 2023 that had lapsed (in part due to health-department/septic issues) and was recently re-approved. The applicant had returned earlier with too many open conditions, so the board had sent them back to tighten the resolution; a revised version removed a good portion of the conditions. The Chair expressed some ambivalence about the concept ('I'm not sure I love it') but made a motion to approve the revised draft resolution, which passed, and then closed the meeting.

memberPositions.evidence: Said 'I'm not sure I love it' and called it 'a bit of an experiment in concept,' but nonetheless moved to approve the revised draft resolution.

meetings.meetingSummary: The Planning Board handled five items: a change-of-use referral for a computer-repair tenant at 70 Lafayette Avenue (sent to the ZBA for a parking variance), a sketch-plan discussion of a residential pool at 250 East Middle Patent Road that the board steered toward a side-yard location to avoid a front-yard variance, a continued discussion of a new house at 700 Bedford Road focused on septic approval and whether to allow two curb cuts (a site walk was scheduled), a wetlands addition at 76 Fireman's Road that the board agreed to schedule for a public hearing, and two extensions of time for the Summit Club subdivision/site plan, which were granted. cases.name: 70 Lafayette Avenue
cases.applicant: Boses (computer-repair tenant); represented by Trevor on behalf of property ownership
cases.summary: A change of use for a roughly 3,300 sq ft space from warehouse to warehouse-plus-work-room, where Boses would repair school-district computer equipment with about five employees on site. cases.name: 250 East Middle Patent Road
cases.applicant: Neil & Vanessa Lucy (owners); attorney Michael Sirignano; landscape architect Jerry Barrett; Nicholas Sarai / Hudson Engineering
cases.summary: A returning application (last seen ~5 years ago under prior owners) for a pool. The applicant presented a new sketch pushing the pool back 16 feet and dropping it about 4 feet so it sits in the side yard on the 75-foot setback line rather than the front yard, eliminating the zoning variance while still requiring scenic-road-overlay and wetland-buffer (150-foot buffer, 25% slopes) attention. The board strongly favored the revised concept, noting it ties the patio to the pool and screens better. They directed the team to formalize the plans with a landscape plan and wetland mitigation plan and return.

Probed where the moved pool sits relative to the steep-slope drop-off and noted the existing stone wall already provides natural screening from the road.

cases.name: 700 Bedford Road
cases.applicant: New-house applicant (owner runs a small business; represented by project engineer/architect)
cases.summary: Continued review of a proposed new house on Route 22. Open issues are whether the Health Department will accept the existing septic (no new septic, which would trigger a wetlands permit), what NYSDOT requires within its right-of-way and for the curb-cut permit, and whether the board will allow two curb cuts where code prefers one. The board pressed on line-of-sight for both driveway openings and questioned the need for two curb cuts, with members floating a single-curb-cut redesign or a parking court. The board scheduled a site walk (a week from Wednesday) and will discuss curb cuts and set a public hearing at the August meeting, targeting possible September approval; a conditional approval tied to the Health Department 'no objection' was discussed.

memberPositions.evidence: Noted the board has previously 'put our foot down' and denied second curb cuts, and pushed to go out and look at the site before deciding; cautioned the applicant not to assume approval.
Suggested a parking court in lieu of a second curb cut to make the house work with a single opening.
Asked for documented line-of-sight measurements from both curb cuts and pressed the applicant to communicate more clearly with the engineer and Health Department.

cases.name: 76 Fireman's Road
cases.applicant: Represented by Alan Piltch, LP Engineering

The plan includes ~16,000+ sq ft of mitigation, invasive-species removal, stormwater controls (rain garden, chambers, pretreatment separator), and driveway screening. cases.name: 1613 Old Orchard Street
cases.applicant: Attorney Wolfson (Hopperman Tortarella & Wexler) for owners Marlene Duran & Diane Rosenberg; engineer Ralph

memberPositions.evidence: Raised the landscape plan, questioning replacement plantings for the ~24 trees removed and urging a landscaping plan be brought to the ARB.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board opened the new academic year by approving the August 11 minutes and moving through four public hearings plus two referral/discussion items. cases.name: 76 Byron Ridge Road
cases.address: 76 Byron Ridge Road (Tax Lot 101.01-2-58, R1A district)
cases.applicant: Alan Piltch (applicant's engineer); property on Byram Lake
cases.summary: Application for a site plan, tree removal permit, and wetlands permit for an addition to an existing three-bedroom single-family house, removal of the existing driveway and construction of a new driveway, with stormwater directed to a rain garden. Tone strongly supportive.

cases.name: 70 Lafayette Avenue — Marquis Associates
cases.applicant: Corey Salamo (Zarin & Steinmetz) and Trevor Tunnel for Marquis Associates
cases.summary: Site plan to convert roughly 3,000 sq ft of existing warehouse space in the building into about 1,002 sq ft of warehouse and 1,698 sq ft of office. cases.name: 1613 Old Orchard Street — new single-family home
cases.address: 1613 Old Orchard Street (Tax Lot 118.03-1-4, R1A district)
cases.applicant: Noel Wolfson (Hopperman, Tortorella & Wexler, counsel), owners Marlene Durand and Diane Rosenberg, and civil engineer Ralph Fensetti
cases.summary: Site plan, tree removal, and wetlands permit for a new two-story four-bedroom colonial (~3,000 sq ft living area, ~4,000 sq ft gross) with a two-car garage on a vacant lot; nearly all disturbance is in the wetland buffer, none in the wetland itself. A neighbor's engineer raised three concerns: whether stormwater design accounted for climate change per the 2024 DEC manual, that the building coverage remained among the largest in the neighborhood despite a 512 sq ft reduction, and driveway sight-line/blind-hill safety. The board treated the driveway as conforming (200-foot sight line plus a ZBA variance), found the footprint reasonable for new construction and consistent on impervious coverage, and, noting the home's 10 Cultec infiltrators exceed neighbors' stormwater controls, closed the hearing and approved a slightly amended resolution conditioned on the DEC wetland permit.

Conservation Board chair Jane Black reiterated concern that the house exceeded the roughly 2,000 sq ft the board had recommended and questioned the buffer impact.

memberPositions.evidence: Argued older homes on the street lack Cultec systems, so with 10 stormwater infiltrators 'this house actually goes well beyond the neighbor's homes in metering out the stormwater'; the Chair thanked him.

Acknowledged the neighbor's concerns but held that 'we can't hold the applicant to a standard that's not applicable to someone else' and that the house 'goes a long way towards addressing the wetlands' and rainfall; found the ~2,000 sq ft footprint reasonable for new construction.

cases.name: 154 Lafayette Avenue parking discussion

cases.name: 4 Vincent Lane driveway modification / site plan clean-up

cases.name: RCLA Enclave at Armonk (former MBIA campus)
cases.applicant: Kevin Moses, attorney for Toll Northeast / Toll Brothers
cases.summary: Toll appealed an RPRC decision (prompted by ARB member Sue Geffen) that referred the applicant back to the ARB to finalize how approved color schemes would be distributed across the 125-unit site. memberPositions.evidence: Wanted to 'placate' the ARB's concerns by having the applicant report progress at one-third, while acknowledging 'when does final mean final' and not holding them rigidly to one-third.
Troubled by revisiting a signed, good-faith contract: 'I just wonder if we're going down a slippery slope, rather than let the contract deliver what he said he was going to deliver.'
Did not want to set a precedent of revisiting signed and sealed deals but was fine with a quick one-third progress report as an update, not something to be re-arbitrated.

cases.name: 92 & 94 Round Hill Road (golf green renovation)
cases.applicant: Owner Michael (Mr. Lair property); attorney; Jerry Barrett (landscape architect); Jim Wollam (golf-pro witness)
cases.status: public hearing continued / adjourned to October 27
cases.summary: Reopened/re-noticed hearing on site plan, wetlands and tree-removal permits to renovate and consolidate private golf greens and tees. The applicant eliminated two new tees, added a buffer/screening plan (12 trees, 54 shrubs, 100 ground covers) and a DEC validation block, and offered a golf pro to argue the short-hole shots pose little risk given 25+ years without incident. Neighbors and their counsel pressed safety concerns about golf balls crossing property lines and asked for netting, a fence, deflector walls and a building-inspector use/setback determination. Because of the short board no vote could be taken; the board discussed deflector screens near the tee boxes as mitigation and adjourned to October 27, leaving the hearing open.
cases.publicComment: Neighbors opposed/concerned but conciliatory. Kalindi Bhat (98 Round Hill Road) questioned whether it was a commercial enterprise and the volume of players. memberPositions.evidence: 'If this were a new application... I would certainly vote no. I think it's a bad precedent and I think it's a safety issue.' Concerned a mis-hit ball could easily cross into the neighbor's yard.

Framed it as a low-intensity recreational suburban use with 25 years of no incidents: 'we're making a mountain out of a molehill'; pushed back on Larry while asking staff to compare the 1998 approval.
Sought mitigation near the tee boxes, asking whether additional plantings or a deflector screen could catch balls hit straight toward the neighbor; open to the project if mitigation is added.

cases.name: 12 Seymour Place East (pool, spa, cabana, carport)

cases.name: 92 & 94 Round Hill Road (putting green and golf tees)
cases.address: 92 & 94 Round Hill Road, North Castle NY
cases.applicant: Attorney Adam Wexler with engineer Tim Allen and landscape architect Jerry Barrett, for owner Mr. Edelman; neighbor represented by attorney Judson C. of Keane & Beane PC
cases.summary: A continued hearing on an existing private putting green and two golf tee boxes in a wetland-buffer area, focused on safety of errant golf balls reaching a neighbor's yard 16 feet from the green. The applicant proposed a localized 10-ft-wide by 6-ft-high net at the upper tee plus deflectors, and after debate agreed to also consider netting at the lower (street) tee and additional evergreen screening. The Chair raised a hypothetical concept of putting-green zoning legislation (setbacks and tee-distance limits) for the town board, which the applicant stressed does not apply to this application. cases.publicComment: The neighbor's attorney (Judson C., Keane & Beane) urged netting be installed at both tees plus additional plantings or a compliant six-foot fence behind the green, and asked to review a revised plan before any vote; tone was cooperative but insistent on protective measures.

Remained concerned even with netting added.

Called legislating tee distances 'a little too onerous / too aggressive' and open to moving greens inland instead; later proposed a row of septic-safe evergreens (green giant/arborvitae) near the street tee for both safety and aesthetics.

Noted the green already has an established approval and focused concern on safety of the neighbor; suggested safety measures at the target/green area, though the board earlier agreed not to build 20-40 ft netting near the green.

Repeatedly asked whether tees could be moved closer to the green to reduce full swings, floated conceptual putting-green legislation for the town board, and pushed to wrap the application up with a revised netting/screening plan and an up-or-down vote at the next meeting.
