cases.name: 76 Virginia Road (National Lawn Sprinkler / Luciano)
cases.address: 76 (74/56) Virginia Road, North White Plains; IND-A zoning district
cases.applicant: John Luciano / National Lawn Sprinkler; attorney Tony Venetano; architect Ron Horenyo; applicant engineer Jose Rodriguez; applicant geotech Carlin Simpson Associates (Bob Simpson serves as the town's retained geotech consultant)
cases.summary: The applicant proposes a 15,000 sq ft office/warehouse building requiring a large rock and soil slope excavation (6-on-1 cuts, 25-ft rock anchors, soil nails, steel mesh netting) 12-15 ft off the property line below the Miller Hill park and battlefield. The applicant's team and the town's geotech consultant (Bob Simpson) reported the applicant met the town's review criteria and that the design is achievable, with only a minor pull-out-strength comment outstanding; the applicant agreed to a no-blasting condition (chipping only) on the site plan. Extensive public opposition and expert critique followed: residents raised fall/safety, catastrophic slope failure, aging/inadequate water and sewer, noise/dust, and the historic significance of Miller Hill, while Conservation Board member Vincent DeAnno gave a detailed technical critique (poor upper rock quality, anchors he believes are too short/undersized, corrosion-protection concerns, ice/rockfall, and long-term maintenance burden potentially falling on the town). The Open Space Committee chair (Carrie Kayza) itemized alleged misrepresentations in the applicant's environmental assessment form (SHPO/archaeology not consulted, historic and critical-environmental-area impacts unaddressed) and asked for alternatives. The board did not close the hearing; it adjourned to a future meeting to address the EAF, ongoing maintenance/deed covenants and bonding, truck logistics, and the town consultant's continuing construction-phase oversight role.
cases.publicComment: Heavy, largely opposed public turnout: residents (George Keller, Kate Hall, Bonnie Fite, Fred Fite, Nora/Norcans, Cynthia Abbott-Coffman) and the Open Space Committee chair raised safety, catastrophic-failure, water/sewer, noise/dust, and especially the loss of the untouched Revolutionary War battlefield; one impassioned historic-preservation plea urged denial. Tone ranged from concerned to strongly opposed, though several acknowledged the owner's property rights.

memberPositions.evidence: Offered zoning/legal framing that catastrophic-failure fears were 'an overstatement' and that the board cannot deprive an owner of legal development rights, yet sharply criticized the 'constant going back and forth and the misinformation being put forth by the applicant' and pressed for a firm no-blasting assurance to be made a condition.

Read the hearing notice, then pressed on who approves in-construction design changes, how the town consultant stays involved, the perpetual maintenance burden if the site is 'mothballed,' and doubted two trucks on site could handle ~2,000 truckloads; asked for a no-trucks-on-street condition.

Asked whether chipping/crushing hour regulations and county air-quality (dust-control water) permits apply, and characterized the session as a 'constructive and meaningful exercise' on a 'difficult and challenging project,' saying real progress was made.

Highlighted resident/Conservation member Vincent DeAnno's 'amazing' underground experience and asked the applicant's engineer whether the design would change based on DeAnno's critique (answer: no), and urged review of the stability calculations.

cases.name: 92 & 94 Round Hill Road
cases.applicant: Applicant represented by attorney Jerry (applicant/principal absent)
cases.summary: The applicant's principal could not attend, so the board reopened and then adjourned the hearing to the second January meeting (Jan 26, 2026) at counsel's request. Counsel noted revised plans that removed the lower 'T' structure entirely, and a neighbor's attorney (George Ellison, for Barry Edelman at 88 Round Hill Road) offered constructive administrative comments: correcting drawing revision dates, papering the T removal in a whereas clause, adding an as-built and an anti-expansion (null-and-void) condition, and exploring whether netting should also run across the top of T2. The board was amenable and set the continued date.
cases.publicComment: Neighbor's attorney (for 88 Round Hill Road) was cooperative and complimentary, offering minor resolution refinements and a netting request rather than opposition.

cases.name: 263 Bedford Banks Road (J. Fane equestrian property)
cases.applicant: Owner represented by attorney Jerry (J. Fane)
cases.summary: Counsel requested a one-year extension of time on an approved equestrian estate (new residence, pool/pool house, renovated exercise barn, second stable, garage with quarters) because the volume of construction cannot be completed in the original 18-month window. The board confirmed the completion clock runs co-terminously with the building permit and granted the one-year extension. Work is reported proceeding in good faith without compliance issues.

cases.name: 4 Vincent Lane (Savage)
cases.applicant: Tom & Savage (owners); landscape architect Lewis Fusco
cases.status: public hearing closed; adjourned pending ARB
cases.summary: A largely restorative wetlands/site-plan project: removing ~25,000 sq ft of lawn/hardscape in a wetland buffer, mitigating with ~40,000 sq ft of wetland planting, removing invasive species and prior owners' astroturf golf features, plus a minor 1,100 sq ft driveway addition. The Conservation Board commended the project. The board closed the public hearing but could not adopt the resolution because pre-existing sheds/barn received building permits but never got Planning Board/ARB sign-off. Sympathetic to the homeowner, the board agreed to send the applicant to the ARB and then approve at a later meeting without requiring the applicant to reappear.
cases.publicComment: No public spoke.

memberPositions.evidence: Objected to burdening a new homeowner 'for a mistake that the town made,' arguing the missing ARB sign-off on pre-existing sheds was a town glitch and pushing for the smoothest path to approve.
Proposed the practical solution of approving after ARB without making the applicant return, noting construction likely wouldn't start until spring anyway.

cases.name: Kent Place Verizon Parking Plan expansion
cases.address: 23 Whipperwill Road East; R-3/4-acre zoning district
cases.applicant: Town of North Castle / Verizon (Kent Place parking)
cases.summary: A re-approval: the previously approved and already-built parking project's approvals lapsed because Verizon never signed the plat map, so the board had to re-run the hearing to file with the health department. An adjacent neighbor (Suzanne) testified that Verizon fails to maintain its side of the property, left a fence down, planted no screening (the neighbor spent ~$40,000 on their own), and removed many trees without replacement, and asked for a few deciduous trees in the corner. The board explained tree replacement was not required and that the downed fence/porta-potty are building-department maintenance matters, then closed the hearing and adopted the negative declaration, site plan, and preliminary and final subdivision resolutions.
cases.publicComment: A 37-year neighbor voiced sustained frustration over Verizon's poor maintenance, lack of screening/tree replacement, a downed fence, and general messiness; board was sympathetic but noted limited jurisdiction and approved the re-application.

cases.name: Almonte-area residential site plan (Angela)
cases.applicant: Angela (owner); engineer absent this meeting
cases.summary: A residential site plan revisited after prior board feedback; the applicant relocated and minimized the pool, pool house, retaining walls, and imported fill to reduce grading, and had wetlands newly flagged in the rear (coordinated between the applicant's wetlands engineer and town engineer Dave). Discussion centered on the cut/fill balance and why the house sits at elevation 473 vs a lower garage grade. The board directed the applicant to answer the planner's and town engineer's memos, meet with staff, and then schedule a public hearing. Constructive tone.

cases.name: 7 Hollow Ridge Road
cases.address: 7 Hollow Ridge Road (Wood Hollow Estates, ~2.5 acre lot)
cases.applicant: Represented by Ralph Alpinsetti; owner/builder John Nickett
cases.summary: A vacant lot from a 1999-2000 subdivision, no wetlands, with public sewer and well water, proposed for a ~7,500-8,000 sq ft house comparable to neighbors. Discussion focused on extensive cut/fill, whether retaining walls could reduce cutting, tree-removal mitigation via landscaping, a rock outcrop that may allow steeper cuts, and building-height rules (average-grade vs lowest-grade measurement) affecting a desired walkout basement. The builder cited prior successful projects on Terrace Circle. The board directed responses to staff memos, a staff meeting, and scheduling a public hearing.

cases.name: IBM EV charger installation (corporate campus)
cases.applicant: IBM (Seth Waltzman and colleague Stephanie)
cases.summary: IBM seeks to install EV chargers in its gated, 24/7-secured visitor lot: three Level 2 units plus one dual Level 3 (fast) charger. Town code currently limits infrastructure to Level 1/2, so the L3 needs a town-board law change (a use variance being a high bar). The board found the L3 sensible given the restricted-access, off-highway location and voted to send a memo recommending the town board amend its law to allow Level 3 charging at this site (a town-board discussion was already agendaed for that Wednesday). Conduit would run mostly above ground with minimal asphalt cutting. The board set the site-plan public hearing for its Jan 12 meeting, planning to approve both L2-only and L2+L3 scenarios.

memberPositions.evidence: Said the L3 charger 'makes all the sense in the world' for this restricted, off-highway site and backed sending a supportive recommendation to the town board.
Argued the gated, manned 24/7 access answers the town's concern about motorists pulling off the highway to fast-charge, strengthening the case for Level 3 here.

cases.name: 113 King Street (airport campus / The Enclave) water tank field change
cases.applicant: Applicant represented by Max Maholic, Cuddy & Feder
cases.summary: A field-change request: due to a CAD/software integration error, the water tank foundation was built about 10 feet north of the approved location, with minor repositioning of the pumping station and generator (the generator still 6 ft from the property line and all elements remaining zoning-compliant). After staff discussions produced a draft resolution, the board adopted it with no questions.

cases.name: 12 Bedford Road
cases.applicant: Owner (the rear-access driveway project)
cases.summary: A brief extension-of-time request on the driveway/rear-access project that is near final approval; the owner is finalizing plans and anxious to proceed. The board granted the extension.

themes.note: Dominant at 76 Virginia Road; also central to 7 Hollow Ridge and the Almonte lot cut/fill debates.
Miller Hill Revolutionary War battlefield/park preservation drove much of the 76 Virginia opposition, including a lengthy plea to deny.
Positive restoration at 4 Vincent Lane; new flagging coordinated at the Almonte lot; mitigation at Kent Place.
Resident testimony about aging, sediment-laden water/sewer infrastructure near 76 Virginia.
Neighbor grievance over Verizon's removed trees and lack of screening; also raised at 7 Hollow Ridge.
Board backed a town-board law change to allow Level 3 chargers at IBM's gated campus.
~2,000 truckloads, queuing, crushing dust control debated at 76 Virginia.
Routine time extensions (263 Bedford Banks, 12 Bedford Road), ARB routing (4 Vincent Lane), field change (113 King St), and Verizon re-approval.

staffInput.summary: Managed plan display and paperwork order throughout; his April 11 memo had raised concern about the extensive slope removal's threat to Miller Hill, and residents cited him when disputing the applicant's characterization of his position. Advised on procedure across cases (ARB routing for 4 Vincent Lane, elevation/cut-fill questions at the Almonte lot and 7 Hollow Ridge, building-permit vs electrical-permit sequencing for IBM, and the Verizon re-approval mechanics).

Referenced as the source of open engineering-review comments (notably on 76 Virginia) and asked to weigh in on the EAF; engineering review threads run through the Almonte lot and 7 Hollow Ridge (via town engineer 'Dave' on wetlands). Generally a technical gatekeeper posture, deferring detailed engineering to post-concept review.

Speaking as a Conservation Board member and 42-year geotech professional, delivered an extended, strongly cautionary critique of the 76 Virginia rock-slope design: poor upper rock quality, anchors he believes are too short and undersized (common rebar, single vs double corrosion protection), crossing fracture planes, line-drill drift, annual ice/rockfall into the parking lot, and a heavy long-term maintenance burden that could fall on the town. Warned this confined neighborhood site is unlike the applicant's large open-area precedents.

meetings.attributionNote: Raw ASR with no speaker labels. The presiding Chair (unnamed) and named readers of hearing notices (Larry Ruizi, Michael Pollock, Steve Sorrell) were identifiable at those moments; Christopher/'Chris' was addressed by name during the 76 Virginia debate. Attributions are medium/low confidence because the Chair and board members frequently overlap in the transcript and public speakers occasionally interject. Town consultant geotech 'Bob Simpson' (Carlin Simpson Associates) is an outside town-retained expert, not a board member. Some applicant/address names are garbled (e.g., the Almonte-area residence and 'National Lawn/Law Sprinkler'); a member 'Tom' is greeted but did not offer a substantive stance.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board handled a full agenda of public hearings and discussion items. It approved an amended site plan for a landscaping tenant at 4 KSL Court, a new single-family home at 62 Nethermont Avenue (after a long debate over rock hammering near a neighbor), and a wetlands mitigation resolution for 88 Byron Ridge Road. It opened and adjourned hearings for 100 Foxout Road and 125 Business Park Drive pending engineering review, approved one of two Massaro Court two-family lots (holding the second for ARB approval), and reviewed early-stage plans for a Coptic church accessibility walkway and a legalization case at 850 North Broadway. An EV charging station application was removed from the agenda.
meetings.durationNote: Board member Larry Ruizi was absent; the Chair and roughly four other members were present with a quorum. A member named 'Tom' also read notices and deliberated but is not on the provided roster.

cases.name: 4 KSL Court
cases.applicant: site engineer for the property owner (name not clearly stated)
cases.summary: The applicant sought an amended site plan to add a landscaping-equipment/vehicle-storage tenant to an existing warehouse building that had never received formal site plan approval. Parking was reworked to eliminate off-property spaces, with dedicated spaces marked for the principal use versus the tenant, and a new lighting design was submitted to meet current code. No members of the public appeared. The board found the resolution clean and approved the amended site plan, with the lighting review satisfying condition number two.
cases.publicComment: No members of the public appeared.

cases.name: 62 Nethermont Avenue
cases.applicant: Rocco Delano (architect) and owners Lindsay & Dmitry; Jim New (seller/family) also spoke
cases.summary: The applicant proposed a new ~4,865 sq ft single-family residence on an oversized R-2F lot, positioned to the south side to preserve a future subdividable lot. Neighbors, especially the Panella/Pinella family, raised concerns about rock excavation/hammering near their century-old rock-founded home, plus house size and neighborhood character; other neighbors spoke in support. The board spent most of its time debating whether to require protections beyond the town's chipping permit given the hammering would occur roughly 53-60 ft from the neighbor's foundation. After input from the applicant, an experienced contractor, and Conservation liaison Vince DeAnno, the board closed the hearing and approved the site plan with amended conditions: a seismic monitor placed on the neighbor's foundation (if they consent) and required line-drilling before chipping to reduce vibration.
cases.publicComment: Emotional and mixed. The Panella/Pinella neighbors feared rock excavation would damage their old rock-founded home; neighbor Nora questioned the house size, tree removal, and its fit with the small-scale neighborhood; the seller (Jim New) and realtor Gail Norris strongly supported the family and argued a single home is far better than the two duplexes he once planned. Tone was earnest but at times tense between the applicant and the board.

memberPositions.evidence: Gave a zoning-style analysis that by preserving the subdividable lot the applicant is 'making a choice' that creates a 'collateral detriment' of hammering six feet from the neighbor, which may warrant a different level of scrutiny than if it were 200 feet away.

Reluctant to make a fully compliant applicant 'jump through extra hoops' beyond existing protections; felt the matter did not rise to a level where standard procedure should be usurped, and proposed drilling before chipping as a workable compromise.
Argued the board was putting 'the cart before the horse' since no chipping permit had been submitted, but ultimately said he could support requiring a seismic monitor on the neighboring foundation.

cases.name: IBM EV Charging Station
cases.summary: The IBM EV charging station application was reached on the agenda but the applicant had removed themselves from the agenda, so no hearing or action took place.

cases.name: 100 Foxout Road
cases.applicant: Nicholas Shri, Hudson Engineering, for the applicant
cases.summary: This R-1A application involves a site plan, wetland permit, and tree removal for a new house. Because the engineer's review memo was still far from resolved, the Chair opened and then adjourned the public hearing to let the applicant work through the memo. The applicant's engineer raised specific points on the NOI/watershed disturbance threshold, driveway drainage constrained by septic setbacks, wetland-buffer mitigation disturbance near the one-acre limit, and rock removal needed on the south side for the sunroom/walkout. The Chair advised tightening the plans and meeting with the town engineer, and noted ARB approval was still needed.
cases.publicComment: No members of the public appeared.

cases.name: 88 Byron Ridge Road
cases.applicant: property owner/applicant team (seeking CO); Jane (consultant) coordinated revisions
cases.summary: This case addressed a wetland-buffer violation: additional disturbance and fill were placed during construction and a required 2022 mitigation plan had gone unimplemented for years. A previously proposed fence and 7,600 sq ft of 'no-mow' lawn were dropped, and the original mitigation plan was installed and verified by the town wetlands consultant, with boulders placed to protect the mitigation area. Conservation liaison Vince DeAnno and Lake Association president Jack expressed frustration over the delays and confusion over how the fence language reached the board's memo, but confirmed the matter was resolved with the town. The board adopted the resolution as amended, adding a clarifying 'whereas' that the fence and placed fill were removed, with five-year monitoring beginning.
cases.publicComment: Conservation liaison Vince DeAnno and Lake Association president Jack were frustrated by years of delay and unimplemented mitigation and wanted assurance the plan would be monitored and stay in place, but were satisfied once the fence/lawn items were removed and mitigation verified.

cases.name: 125 Business Park Drive
cases.address: 125 Business Park Drive, Lot 5 Westchester Business Park (tax map 108.03-1-55)
cases.applicant: applicant seeking reapproval of previously approved plans
cases.summary: The applicant sought reapproval of a previously approved (now expired) site plan for an approximately 9,390 sq ft warehouse/office commercial building with parking and loading in the PLI zoning district. The Chair read the notice, opened the public hearing, and immediately adjourned it with no substantive discussion.

cases.name: 2 & 4 Massaro Court
cases.address: Massaro Court (tax map 122.12-3-8.1 and related lots)
cases.applicant: applicant's site engineer and architect (Rick, engineer, commented)
cases.summary: This R-2F application covers site plan and steep-slope approval for two two-family residences on adjacent Massaro Court lots. The applicant addressed prior comments by reworking the driveway retaining wall into a terraced design, adding dedicated parking so each unit has two spaces, revising side/rear grading, and clarifying footing-drain discharge. Remaining engineering memo items were deemed handleable administratively, and the town planner and engineer were comfortable. The board closed the hearings and approved the resolution for 4 Massaro Court tonight, agreeing that 2 Massaro Court (identical building) would be approved administratively at a future meeting once the applicant obtains ARB approval, with a note to watch for possible rock during the ~8 ft driveway cut.
cases.publicComment: No members of the public appeared.

cases.name: Virgin Mary & St. Monique Coptic Orthodox Church
cases.applicant: clergy/representatives of the Coptic Orthodox Church
cases.summary: The church proposed a level sidewalk/walkway across its own lot to provide accessible access to the lower level of the 30-year-old church for elderly and disabled parishioners, cutting through soil behind an existing retaining wall without altering the building's exterior or the wall's appearance. The Chair asked whether an ADA ramp to the upper level was feasible; the applicants explained the upper level's many steps made that impractical, so the level walkway to the lower-level entrance is the goal. Because nothing on the building is changing, the planner concluded no ARB approval and no new variances are needed, and directed the applicant to meet with staff and schedule a public hearing.

cases.name: 850 North Broadway
cases.applicant: property owner (not present)
cases.summary: Work was done on the back of the building without a permit and now needs to be legalized, along with related site plan issues. The applicant was not present. The planner explained that, similar to the 4 KSL Court approach, the applicant will need to submit a basic site plan showing refuse handling, parking, and lighting to reach a position where the board can approve a site plan. No action was taken beyond noting next steps.

themes.note: Dominated the 62 Nethermont hearing; board debated protections beyond the chipping permit and recurred as a caution at Foxout, Massaro, and Byron Ridge.
Central to 88 Byron Ridge (violation resolved) and a concern at 100 Foxout's buffer disturbance.
62 Nethermont's placement to preserve a future subdividable lot drove much of the debate.
Neighbors questioned the scale of the 62 Nethermont home; applicant argued it is FAR-compliant and in line with recent builds.
Footing drains and driveway drainage discussed at Massaro Court and Foxout Road.
Coptic church accessible walkway received a favorable, low-conflict review.
Raised at 62 Nethermont and part of the 100 Foxout application.

staffInput.summary: Confirmed paperwork was in order for each case and steered procedure throughout. At 62 Nethermont he explained the house is below the FAR/coverage threshold adopted after the mid-2000s teardown debate, offered to research how the board handled seismic monitoring at the earlier 22 Nethermont case, and framed how a drilling/monitor condition could be built into the resolution and chipping permit. He advised tightening the Foxout memo, clarified the Byron Ridge mitigation history and resolution amendment, was comfortable with Massaro Court, told the church it needs no ARB approval or new variances, and outlined the basic site plan needed to legalize 850 North Broadway.

Provided the consulting engineering review memos underlying several cases. His office's comments drove the adjournment of 100 Foxout Road (NOI/watershed, driveway drainage, wetland-buffer disturbance, rock removal) and the outstanding-but-administrative items at Massaro Court (drain sizes, peak flows, landscaping detail, plus a caution to watch for rock in the ~8 ft driveway cut). His office also handled the Byron Ridge fill remediation.

As Conservation Board liaison he detailed the Byron Ridge wetland-violation history, objected to how the dropped fence and 7,600 sq ft no-mow lawn had appeared in the memo, and confirmed the mitigation plan was installed, boulder-protected, and entering five-year monitoring. He also stepped in as a de facto geotechnical resource at 62 Nethermont (a civil engineer with a geotech background), explaining seismograph thresholds, line-drilling to reduce vibration, and that at ~50+ ft a small hammer would likely not be a concern.

meetings.attributionNote: The presiding Chair speaks most and was reliably identifiable; members were named when reading notices (Michael Pollock, Steve Sorrell, Tom, and the Chair). The Chair's and Christopher's voices blur during the 62 Nethermont rock-hammering debate, lowering confidence on which of them made specific zoning-analysis statements. A board member 'Tom' (surname possibly 'Crispy') read notices and backed Steve's proposal but is not on the provided roster, so his stances were not recorded as memberPositions. Larry Ruizi was absent. Outside participants included architect Rocco Delano, engineer Nicholas Shri (Hudson Engineering), a contractor 'Rick' who gave rock-removal expertise, and Lake Association president Jack; several neighbor surnames (Panella/Pinella, Norris) were garbled in the ASR.

meetings.meetingSummary: Despite a snowstorm and prior state of emergency, the North Castle Planning Board held its scheduled meeting to avoid forcing applicants to re-notice public hearings. The board opened/adjourned a hearing for a new home at 7 Hallowell Road (awaiting a landscape plan and ARB approval), approved a site plan and tree removal for 3 Israel Tomahsen Hill, and approved amended site plan for IBM EV charging stations. It spent most of the evening on the 76 Virginia Road rock-cut retaining wall application (adopting an amended Negative Declaration but keeping the hearing open over seismic monitoring, bonding, deed restrictions, and truck staging), gave brief updates on the 825 North Broadway gas station and a field change at 26 Hurlingham Drive, and debated then declined to comment on a town-board referral of a proposed local law allowing Level 3 EV charging.
meetings.durationNote: Meeting held during snow emergency; Michael Pollock attended by Zoom; quorum present. Larry noted absent from the prior (Jan 12) meeting's minutes vote.

cases.name: 7 Hallowell Road
cases.address: 7 Hallowell Road (tax lot 100.02-1-41), R28 zoning district
cases.applicant: Ralph (applicant's engineer/representative); landscape plan by Steve Lopez
cases.summary: A new single-family residence and associated tree removal proposed on a 2.5-acre vacant lot in an improved subdivision, connecting to sewer with a proposed well and front/rear stormwater mitigation. A neighbor at 6 Hallowell Place (Deb and Marie) emailed concerns about tree removal and screening. The board noted the landscape plan was missing from the submission and that ARB approval is still pending (expected next week). The Chair moved to adjourn the public hearing to await the landscape plan and the applicant's return, when the neighbor's concerns can be addressed.
cases.publicComment: No residents spoke in person; a neighbor at 6 Hallowell Place submitted a letter objecting to tree removal and lack of screening, to be addressed at a future hearing.

memberPositions.evidence: Would not close the hearing without seeing the landscape plan, noting it 'might impact how we address some of the comments from the neighbor.'

cases.name: 3 Israel Tomahsen Hill
cases.address: 3 Israel Tomahsen Hill (tax lot 108.01-6-1.2), R1A zoning district
cases.applicant: Andrew Vaccariello, Federal Engineering (applicant team from the 32 Orchard Drive subdivision)
cases.summary: Third application from the existing 32 Orchard Drive subdivision, this one for the lot with the existing dwelling to remain, adding a driveway off the cul-de-sac, relocating the well, abandoning the old septic system, and directing runoff to the shared stormwater basin. The engineer reported 17 trees for removal, minimized steep-slope encroachment, and full zoning compliance. Larry asked about the septic-area tree buffer and confirmed a vegetated buffer between lots. The town engineer confirmed all comments were addressed; the board closed the hearing and approved the site development plan and tree removal permit.
cases.publicComment: No members of the public were present for this application.

memberPositions.evidence: Asked about plantings near the septic/property line and the tree buffer to the adjacent future lot; satisfied by answers and moved the approval resolution.

cases.name: IBM EV Charging Stations
cases.address: 1 New Orchard Road (tax lot 113.02-1-8), OB zoning district
cases.applicant: IBM (world headquarters); applicant representative present
cases.summary: IBM sought amended site plan approval to install four EV charging stations in its gated visitor parking lot. Current town code prohibits Level 3 chargers, so the board approved the installation as Level 2 for now, with the ability to build Level 3 if the town board later adopts the pending code change without returning to the Planning Board. Staff described it as a simple application with no planning concerns. The hearing was opened, no public spoke, and the board closed it and adopted the resolution.
cases.publicComment: No members of the public were present for this application.

cases.name: 76 Virginia Road (rock-cut retaining/wall system)
cases.applicant: Tony (Anthony) Viziano, attorney; Jose Rodriguez, CC Engineering; wall/geotech consultant
cases.status: public hearing continued (kept open/adjourned); Negative Declaration adopted as amended
cases.summary: The applicant returned on the proposal to cut into a rock hillside behind an office building, submitting a Phase 1A archaeological report (no/low sensitivity, accepted by SHPO) to resolve the historic-value question. Extensive deliberation covered a required seismic/vibration monitoring plan, perpetual maintenance via a deed restriction and bond, and staging of an estimated 20 trucks/day for months on Virginia Road. Two residents spoke critically: the North Castle Historical Society flagged an inaccurate letter reference in the Negative Declaration (removed by amendment), and Vincent Giordano challenged anchor lengths, ice/safety, and whether the project is really a rock quarry. The board adopted the amended Negative Declaration but kept the public hearing open, directing the applicant to bring back a written monitoring plan for the town engineer's review, a truck-staging plan, and bonding/insurance details for repair/repinning.
cases.publicComment: Two residents spoke critically: North Castle Historical Society's Edward (past president) objected to an inaccurate letter cited in the Neg Dec; Vincent Giordano argued the north/south anchors (15 ft and 10 ft) are too short, raised ice/crash-barrier safety concerns, questioned an alternate design, and suggested the excavation functions as a quarry to sell rock. Tone was skeptical to opposed.

memberPositions.evidence: Argued a $5,000 maintenance bond is helpful but insufficient because the risk goes beyond maintenance; pressed for a bond covering the cost of repair/repinning in the event of a wall failure, since insurance would not cover it.
Not comfortable closing the hearing with the public absent; drove resolution of monitoring, maintenance, and staging issues but expressed willingness to keep the application moving.
Worried about queuing/staging trucks and protecting Virginia Road from cars driving around trucks; pushed for a staging plan written into the resolution.

cases.name: 825 North Broadway (gas station)
cases.applicant: not stated
cases.summary: Staff gave a brief status update on the gas station application. A draft resolution had been prepared, but too many engineering comments remained outstanding for the town engineer to recommend adoption. The applicant addressed many conditions in a subsequent submission but not enough, and will make another submission. No action was taken.

cases.name: 26 Hurlingham Drive (field change)
cases.applicant: applicant's representative (project first before board around 2021)
cases.summary: The applicant sought a field change to reconfigure the driveway serving the caretaker's residence and main house, eliminating a looping driveway in favor of a more direct approach. Board members had no comments or questions and praised the design. The board approved the field change, noting the resolution's property address needed to be updated.

memberPositions.evidence: 'Nice design'; had no comments or questions and moved approval.

cases.name: Level 3 EV Charging Local Law (town board referral)
cases.applicant: Town Board (referral of proposed local law)
cases.status: referred back to town board with no recommendation
cases.summary: The town board referred a proposed local law to permit currently-prohibited Level 3 EV charging, with an open question of whether Level 3 spaces should count toward off-street parking requirements (a draft cap of no more than 20%). Members debated at length: some favored reducing barriers and counting EV spaces within the parking requirement, while others raised concerns about parking capacity, the town becoming a highway 'road stop,' and a 'backdoor' path to for-profit charging. Lacking enough information to endorse a position, the board voted to send the referral back to the town board as written, with no further comment.

memberPositions.evidence: Initially leaned toward recommending inclusion in the parking count but concluded he did not know enough, and was comfortable sending the law back to the town board as written with no comment.
Noted many parking situations are already at their limit, so counting EV spaces could inhibit installations; wary of unintended consequences.
Asked practical questions about siting/proximity of chargers and where the power would come from; treated the details as largely beyond the board's scope.

themes.note: 76 Virginia Road dominated the meeting: anchor lengths, ice, netting, wall failure risk.
IBM chargers approved; extended, unresolved debate over Level 3 local law and parking counts.
Debate over whether a maintenance bond covers repair/repinning; deed restriction to bind future owners.
~20 trucks/day on Virginia Road; board wants a staging plan in the resolution.
Neighbor concerns at 7 Hallowell Road; 17 trees and buffers discussed at 3 Israel Tomahsen Hill.
Phase 1A report accepted by SHPO; Historical Society corrected a Neg Dec letter reference.
Recurring across residential site plans (Hallowell, Israel Tomahsen Hill).

staffInput.summary: Introduced each application and framed the procedural path: noted pending ARB approval and neighbor email for 7 Hallowell Road; structured the IBM approval as Level 2 now with Level 3 contingent on the town board's code change; advised the amended Negative Declaration could be adopted without waiting on further SHPO confirmation; explained the gas station's outstanding conditions; and walked the board through the Level 3 EV local law referral and the off-street-parking question.

Confirmed the 3 Israel Tomahsen Hill applicant had addressed all engineering comments and concerns; for 76 Virginia Road the board designated him to review and critique the applicant's forthcoming seismic monitoring plan; found too many outstanding comments to recommend adopting the 825 North Broadway gas station resolution.

cases.name: 7 Hollow Ridge Road
cases.applicant: Property owner (Charlie Katch); Lauren Brennan, engineer (Alton Engineering); a landscape architect on the team
cases.summary: Continuation of a public hearing for a single-family house with a proposed pool, patio, driveway and stormwater mitigation. The applicant reported reducing disturbance from ~71,700 to ~62,000 sq ft, adding a rear retaining wall, and cutting tree removals from 134 to 99. Most of the session walked through the town engineer's (John Kellard's) memo, which the applicant had not yet seen: grading of a rear knoll, up-to-10-foot driveway cuts and rock, sediment/erosion control (a temporary sediment trap instead of just silt fence), and trench drains on the 14% driveway. Board decided the applicant should take the memo home, revise the plans, and return for a final resolution; the hearing was adjourned but left open.
cases.publicComment: No members of the public spoke; the applicant/owner was audibly frustrated at further delay ("I've had this for about four months... I'm just anxious to go to work") after four months and prior cancellations.

memberPositions.evidence: Sympathetic to the applicant grading out the knoll to level the property ('it seemed reasonable to me'), but insisted the applicant must review and address the engineer's memo before a resolution, saying it wouldn't be appropriate to adopt a resolution the applicant hasn't seen.

Said it makes sense for the applicant to meet with the engineer and work everything out before returning, rather than the board solving all issues at the table; separately defended white pines as effective screening from his own property experience.

cases.name: 124 Kisco Road
cases.summary: Brief status update and extension of time. The applicant is still awaiting final Health Department sign-off, and the town engineer is finalizing review to confirm completeness. Board granted the extension of time.

cases.name: 154 Lafayette Avenue
cases.applicant: Mark (representative) for Mike Mealy; owners present
cases.summary: Change of use of a legal non-conforming home to office use, with a related lot-line/subdivision consolidating three parcels (removing one dwelling, moving a property line). The recurring sticking point had been parking, especially six parallel spaces at the street plus 16 truck-storage spaces in back. Board confirmed no exterior changes (so no ARB needed) and worked through whether ZBA relief was required, concluding the non-conformity isn't being increased (a building-inspector determination). The condition to show nine required off-street office spaces (kept truck-free) was refined, an ARB condition struck, and the board adopted the negative declaration plus site plan and preliminary/final subdivision resolutions.
cases.publicComment: No members of the public appeared for the hearing.

memberPositions.evidence: Offered the zoning analysis that moving the property line is acceptable so long as it doesn't increase the non-conformity (e.g., adding an apartment), which would trigger ZBA review; framed it as a building-inspector determination.
Pressed on the parking arithmetic and expressly permitting overnight truck storage on the balance of spaces beyond the nine required office spaces; ultimately signaled he was okay with it.

cases.name: 124/125 Business Park Drive
cases.summary: A previously approved application that had expired and required re-approval. Since the earlier approvals (originally ~2006, re-approved ~2008/2010) the applicant obtained fresh ZBA approval. The board reopened and closed the public hearing, confirmed the wetland-buffer regulations had not changed since the prior approvals (so the same requirements apply), and adopted the negative declaration and draft resolution.
cases.publicComment: No members of the public appeared.

memberPositions.evidence: Asked whether the wetland-buffer regulations had changed since the prior resolution; satisfied on confirmation that the buffers remained the same and the same requirements apply.

cases.name: 23 North Lake
cases.applicant: Conrad Rancotti, project architect; owner Mr. Haber (site engineer and landscape designer on team)
cases.summary: Discussion of a proposed new four-bedroom house on a steep, partly wetland site with an existing (never-used) pool and septic field to be reused. The item before the board was a retaining wall exceeding six feet (up to ~10.17 ft, retaining ~7.17 ft of soil) at the front of a courtyard, faced in native stone. The architect also floated a possible modification relocating the detached one-car garage next to the two-car garage, with a reduced two-car garage mass and a breezeway. Stormwater, driveway grading and septic re-certification with the Health Department were touched on. Applicant still must finish with the Conservation Board (wetlands, meeting on the 17th) and return to the ARB before a public hearing is scheduled. The Chair recused himself and stepped down for this item.

memberPositions.evidence: Called it 'an attractive design,' said it's the homeowner's home and they have to be happy with it, engaged constructively on breaking up the garage mass and mitigating wall height with landscaping.

cases.name: City (directional signage)
cases.applicant: Sign contractor (traveled from Long Island)
cases.summary: Applicant sought to replace directional signs at 36x20 inches, exceeding the one-square-foot limit for directional signage. The board explained it cannot grant that exception; the ZBA must approve additional sign area first, after which the Planning Board can approve the site plan for the freestanding signs (building signs handled separately). Board voted to refer the applicant to the ZBA.

cases.name: NYC DEP Wetland Mitigation Project (KEC / Kensico-Eastview Connection)
cases.address: Route 120 access; staging at Old Post Road (Block 1, Lots 15 & 16)
cases.applicant: NYC Department of Environmental Protection (Angel Riness, Arne Farath and team)
cases.summary: DEP presented a wetland mitigation project tied to the Kensico-Eastview Connection tunnel and a related shoreline stabilization (in Mount Pleasant). On a 6.4-acre DEP parcel, ~2.5 acres of wetland (aquatic/shallow-emergent marsh, high marsh, open water) plus ~1.7 acres of upland habitat would be created, requiring removal of ~388 trees and ~9,478 herbaceous plants/shrubs, with a ~1-acre staging area (only ~5 trees removed there, none over 24 inches). Construction traffic estimated at ~3 trucks per peak hour, work hours 7am-3pm per the noise ordinance, with mechanical rock removal and blasting as an option. Board asked about blasting radius and nearby houses/underground infrastructure; finding it largely procedural, referred the applicant to the Conservation Board.

memberPositions.evidence: Diligent but supportive: asked about the blasting impact radius, nearby houses and underground infrastructure, then moved to refer the project to the Conservation Board as procedural.

cases.name: Vincent Lane
cases.summary: The board had previously closed the public hearing and directed the applicant to obtain ARB approval before returning for adoption. With the ARB approval now in hand, the board adopted the draft resolution without further discussion.

cases.name: Short-Term Rental Law (town referral)
cases.applicant: Town of North Castle (Town Board)
cases.status: reviewed; returned to Town Board with no comment
cases.summary: The Town Board referred its proposed short-term-rental law to the Planning Board because it amends the zoning chapter. The planner explained it sets up the regulatory framework (operating permit, building-department inspections, day limits, quiet hours, occupancy tax, primary-residence requirement) and largely doesn't affect the Planning Board. The board debated at length: enforcement/compliance difficulty, the primary-residence requirement, and the provision barring a short-term rental on the same lot as an accessory apartment (ADU). After roughly 15 minutes the board reviewed it and voted to send it back to the Town Board with no substantive comment, deferring to the Town Board's research.

memberPositions.evidence: Argued the regulation is legitimate by analogy to hotels, which have stricter fire codes and supervision absent in short-term rentals, so the need to know where they occur and to protect occupants and neighbors is real.

Worried the law is too cumbersome, onerous and complex, and that in trying to cover all bases the Town Board might inadvertently defeat its purpose by discouraging owners from seeking operating permits and complying.
Read the law as the town deliberately discouraging short-term rentals without outright banning them (primary-residence requirement plus the ADU restriction), and was okay with that approach.
Pushed back on making the law briefer, warning that openings invite people to run through them and that vagueness would be harder to enforce and more chaotic; didn't mind the law's extent/complexity.

cases.name: Bucks Flower Garden, 65 Bedford Road
cases.applicant: Whitney Singleton, attorney; Joe Rina, engineer (client owns wholesale nursery ~46 years, not present)
cases.summary: A long-running enforcement/cleanup matter for a wholesale nursery and single-family home with several violations: unpermitted fill (~700+ cubic yards) with a boulder retaining wall, an unpaved loop road, and a lapsed sign permit. The attorney is trying to resolve pending Justice Court litigation by getting the site legalized; the applicant is reducing wholesale-nursery scope and abandoning retail while adding a new home and barn/office buildings. The planner's memo argues the modifications require Town Board re-review of the special use permit on intensity-of-use grounds, which the attorney contests. Board wants a narrative of operations, soil/core sampling for possible fill contamination (coordinated via HES), and scheduled a site walk for April 8 at 8:30am (while leaves are off the trees) before further review. DEC has signed off on re-flagged wetlands and found no violations.

memberPositions.evidence: Invoked the board's strong precedent for how it has handled fill before, noting the area's environmental sensitivity ('It's a critical environmental area') while not opposing moving forward with soil testing.
Wanted to revisit the site with a site walk and get an operations narrative before judging the intensity-of-use question and the fill/contamination protocol; cooperative but non-committal.

cases.name: 40 High Street
cases.summary: Subdivision extension of time; applicant still awaiting the Health Department. Board granted the extension without concern.

cases.name: 298 Bedford Banksville Road

cases.name: 7 Hollow Ridge Road
cases.applicant: Lauren (project engineer), with Rick and Ralph; landscape architect (screening)
cases.summary: Resumed public hearing on a site plan with significant grading and drainage. The Chair declined to approve because the revised plans were not yet formalized and the tree impacts undefined, sending the applicant back to perfect the drawings with the engineer before returning.
cases.publicComment: A neighbor (Steve Lopez) asked about screening-tree placement within the conservation setback; board confirmed screening is permitted there. A prior neighbor letter about screening was addressed by a landscaping condition.

memberPositions.evidence: Felt it was 'asking too much of the planning board' to accept unformalized plans; 'historically we wouldn't approve this without these details in order,' and sent the applicant home to perfect the plans.
Probed the trench-drain sump structure and the drainage behind the retaining wall, noting eliminating the wall would require another set of engineer-reviewed drawings.

cases.name: 76 Virginia Road (National Lawn Services / Spring Court)
cases.applicant: National Lawn Services; attorneys Anthony and Tom; engineer Jose Rodriguez (SESC); architect Ron Hoin; town's reviewing geotech Bob/Colin Simpson (Carlin Simpson Associates)
cases.summary: Resumed public hearing on a 0.94-acre, ~15,700 sf building for a landscaping business (indoor truck/equipment parking plus office), requiring a large rock cut with 70-foot cuts, a stabilized rock wall (chipping, not blasting; not crushing on site) and a truck-routing plan queuing trucks off-site. The board dwelled at length on insurance/liability for potential future wall or slope failure, concluding contractor, engineer and owner policies apply and that the residual risk is covered via the operating agreement/maintenance manual traveling with the deed, with a 'reasonable' insurance requirement to be baked into the building department's operating permit. It reviewed the upgraded seismic/vibration/air/noise monitoring plan (stop-work exceedance alerts emailed to the town's building and engineering departments and Carlin Simpson) and a Phase 1B archaeology report finding no sensitivity on-site (with notable Battle of White Plains findings on the adjacent Miller Hill Park). The board closed the hearing and adopted the draft resolution as amended, referencing the new Phase 1B document.
cases.publicComment: No members of the public spoke; a resident (Nora) reportedly watched on television and had previously expressed interest.

memberPositions.evidence: Pressed hard on catastrophic/uninsurable failure risk and who maintains the slope decades out if an owner walks away; ultimately 'satisfied with the answer... I just want everyone to be aware of the risk... all be it remote.'
Called the Phase 1B 'impressive' and commended the client's patience and the team's cooperation; urged that adequate owner insurance be a condition of the operating permit.
Praised the applicant's and town's due diligence and 'a monitoring plan that should work well for the town,' noting it is a lawful, if unconventional, building lot before adopting the resolution.

cases.name: Church special-use permit referral (ADA sidewalk)

The board voted a positive recommendation to the town board so the sidewalk site plan can proceed.

The board directed the applicant to ARB, after which it will return for a public hearing and approval.

memberPositions.evidence: Noted the landscaping plan had been enhanced and comments straightened out with the town engineer; 'Everything looks like it's an award, excellent,' then moved to close the hearing and adopt the resolution.

cases.name: 100 Buckout Road
cases.applicant: Nicholas Shariah, Hudson Engineering, for owner Mr. Mulliek Samad
cases.summary: Continuation of a public hearing on a new residence involving steep-slope disturbance and wetland-buffer impacts. The applicant's engineer argued that repeated KSCJ memo conditions (retaining wall, tree counts, earthwork, soil testing, infiltration/stormwater) had already been addressed and asked for a vote, but the board would not approve. A roughly one-acre wetland-buffer mitigation had been steered toward administrative handling after a site walk, which the board and staff agreed was improper since only the board can direct that; the mitigation plan must instead go to the Conservation Board and the hearing be re-noticed. Sympathetic to the owner's frustration ('you have the right to be upset') but firm that an error was made, that the board should not 'double down,' and that the mitigation plan must go to the Conservation Board with the hearing re-noticed before any approval.

cases.name: Bezel Residence, Six Ledge Place
cases.applicant: Bezel (owner); represented by an engineer (Charles) of Cola engineering
cases.summary: Discussion of proposed exterior improvements around the house, including significant retaining walls (6 to 13 ft), a sports court, pergola, and fire pit on a steep-sloped site. cases.name: Kensico-Eastview Connection Project - Big Peninsula & Old Post Road Wetland Mitigation
cases.address: Kensico River and Old Post Road (parcels 25 & 27 Old Post Road); tax parcels 113.01-1-1-1 and 113.02-1-15-16; R2A and PB-O zoning districts
cases.applicant: New York City Department of Environmental Protection (DEP); presenter Angel Vides with full design/construction/EP team
cases.summary: The board opened a public hearing on the DEP's KEC wetland mitigation program, which includes shoreline stabilization near the upper effluent chamber and creation of roughly 2.5 acres of wetland at the Big Peninsula, plus a one-acre construction staging area at Old Post Road. The applicant presented the tunnel/redundancy rationale, tree clearing and replanting counts, and traffic estimates (up to three peak-hour construction vehicles, work hours 7-3 per the town noise ordinance) running fall 2026 through ~2029-2031. The Conservation Board reported it had done a lengthy site walk and gave a positive recommendation, and the town planner said the submission was thorough with no significant concerns and that engineer/consultant comments were folded into the resolution. The board adopted SEQRA findings identical to DEP's and approved the site plan, wetlands, and tree removal permits; DEP committed to quarterly updates to the town via Adam Kaufman.
cases.publicComment: One resident, Zach Haas of Whippoorwill Road, spoke - not against the project but to raise an urgent safety concern about the Whippoorwill/King Street hairpin turn worsened by regional construction traffic; his tone was earnest and concerned. The board was sympathetic but explained there was no real nexus between the wetland project and that state-road intersection.

memberPositions.evidence: Praised DEP's comparable 'bowling alley' mitigation project as amazing and impressive, said he brings people to see it, and moved to adopt findings and approve the permits.

Related to the resident's Whippoorwill/King Street concern ('I live up... I know exactly what you're talking about'), cautioned about making the right turn there, but agreed the board's leverage over the state road was limited.

cases.name: Social Life Members Club (Cigar Lounge)
cases.address: 909 & 911 North Broadway; tax lot 122.12-4-52; CP zoning district
cases.applicant: Social Life Members Club applicant (cigar/membership lounge operator)
cases.summary: The board opened a public hearing on a change-of-use site development plan for the Social Life Members Club, a cigar and membership lounge in a shopping center. The planner explained the applicant had already obtained its special use permit and that, based on the prior bakery use and the shopping center parking calculation using the one-space-per-three-seats standard (17 spaces), no off-street parking variance was needed, making this a simple change of use with no physical changes. Board banter touched on a Seinfeld reference; members asked about liquor licensing and tiered memberships. The public hearing was closed and the change-of-use site plan approved.

memberPositions.evidence: Wished the applicant well repeatedly ('I wish you well, I really do... any business enterprise') and moved the approval along.

themes.note: DEP Big Peninsula wetland mitigation was the centerpiece and well received.
Resident concern over the Whippoorwill/King Street hairpin dominated the DEP hearing discussion; board sympathetic but felt limited.
Rip-rap hardening to keep debris/runoff out of the reservoir, tied to the wetland mitigation.
Trees cleared for the project offset by replanting (e.g., 24 trees planted at the staging area).

staffInput.summary: Called the DEP submission thorough with no significant concerns, noted DEP has done similar projects in town, and updated the draft resolution to incorporate the town engineer and consultant memo comments; designated as the town's point of contact for DEP's quarterly updates. For the cigar lounge, explained the special use permit was already granted, that the parking calculation under the shopping center avoided any variance, and that it was a simple change of use.

Speaking for the Conservation Board, reported the applicant had presented twice and that the board did a lengthy site walk of the entire property; the board was very pleased with the mitigation, had a few minor comments that were resolved, and gave a positive recommendation.
